title: France – Parts of escalators – Fourniture des pièces détachées diverses pour la maintenance des escaliers mécaniques de la RATP
description: La présente consultation a pour objet la fourniture de pièces détachées diverses pour la maintenance patrimoniale et courante des escaliers mécaniques. La consultation concerne la mise en place d’un ou plusieurs accords-cadres à commande, elle concerne la fourniture de 200 références de pièces détachées diverses pour les EM CNIM, OTIS, KONE et THYSSEN. Il s’agit d’un ou plusieurs accords-cadres à bons de commande avec montant minimum et maximum. Le marché est conclu pour une durée de 60 mois ferme, à compter de la date du 1er Ordre de Livraison ou de Service (OLS) émis par la RATP. Le marché est alloti en 200 lots. Chaque référence est égale à 1 lot en phase procédure mais la contractualisation se fait par fournisseur proposant l'offre économiquement la plus avantageuse sur les lots faisant l'objet de son positionnement. Aucune limitation du nombre de lots susceptibles d'être attribués à un même soumissionnaire n'est prévue. Par conséquent, un même opérateur économique peut se voir attribuer un seul lot, plusieurs lots ou l'ensemble des lots pour lesquels il a remis l'offre économiquement la plus avantageuse, sous réserve de la conformité de sa candidature et de son offre. La RATP ne fixe donc aucun nombre minimum ni maximum de lots pouvant être attribués à un même candidat

title: Germany – Installation of fitted kitchens – Küchentechnik
description: Auf dem innerstädtischen Grundstück der Königsegg-Grundschule in Immenstadt wird die bestehende Sporthalle zurückgebaut und durch einen Ersatzneubau mit Sporthalle, Verwaltung für Schule und Hort, Kinderhort und Mensa ersetzt. Die beengte innerstädtische Lage erfordert eine kompakte Lösung am Standort der bisherigen Halle. Im Neubau entstehen eine Einfeldsporthalle mit Nebenräumen im Untergeschoss, Verwaltungsräume für Schule und Hort im Erdgeschoss sowie ein zweigeschossiger Hortbereich für ca. 250 Kinder in den beiden Obergeschossen. Eine Mensa mit Küche für ca. 105 Kinder befindet sich ebenfalls im 2. OG. Die Nutzung erfolgt durch Grundschule, Hort und Ganztagsklassen. Die Anbindung an den Bestand erfolgt barrierefrei mit einem neuen Aufzug im Neubau. Begleitende Umbauten im Schulgebäude ermöglichen die Umnutzung bestehender Horträume für Ganztagsklassen. Die Fachräume im UG-Bestand bleiben erhalten und stehen ebenfalls auch dem Hort zur Verfügung. Der Neubau wird in Massiv- und Holzbauweise errichtet. Die Sporthalle und das EG bestehen aus Stahlbeton, die Obergeschosse aus Holzrahmen- und Holztafelbau. Das Dach ist als versetztes Pultdach mit Gründach und Blechdeckung ausgeführt. Die Fassade kombiniert Faserzementplatten und Holzverkleidung. Die Außenanlagen werden neu strukturiert. Es entstehen eingefriedete Freiflächen für Schule und Hort, sowie ein neuer Allwetterplatz. Ausgeschrieben wird diese Maßnahme in Einzelgewerken.

title: C1DA--VISN 5 - INDEFINITE DELIVERY INDEFINITE QUANTITY ARCHITECT & ENGINEERING CONTRACT
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE FOR 36C24526R00107, INDEFINITE DELIVERY INDEFINITE QUANTITY ARCHITECT & ENGINEERING CONTRACT (IDIQ A&E) FOR ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR VETERANS INTEGRATED SERVICE NETWORK (VISN) 5 The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 5, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 5 has a requirement for on-going engineering services at medical facilities within the aforementioned VISN. The intent of the project is to award multiple Architect & Engineering Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity for the Veterans Affairs Maryland Healthcare System (VAMHCS), VA Medical Centers in West Virginia and VA Medical Centers in Washington, D.C, to include any Community Based Clinics supported by the aforementioned. The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS Code) 541330 (Engineering Services). This is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set aside procurement. The Small Business Size Standard is $25.5 million. The term of the A&E IDIQ will be for ten years from date of award. The resulting contracts will have fixed unit costs. Under the A&E IDIQ, all contract work will be completed through individual task orders awarded for individual projects in VISN 5/NCO 5. All work will be in accordance with individual task order requirements, including but not limited to specifications and drawings are to be provided for each project. Each task order will be priced individually using the agreed-upon wage determinations and period of performance. These task orders will be competed amongst the IDIQ awardees. The overall value of the A&E IDIQ contracts shall not exceed $450 million over the ten-year period. This amount is inclusive of all awardees. Individual task orders will be firm fixed price, with a minimum task order value of $2,500.00 and maximum of $2 million. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this solicitation will be a 100% Total Set-Aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses must be registered and verified in the VetBiz Registry in order to be eligible for contract award. Visit www.vip.vetbiz.gov to complete your company s registration. In accordance with FAR RFO 52.204-7, System for Award Management Contractor Registration, 52.102(a)(4) Annual Representation and Certification and in accordance with FAR RFO 2.101, prospective contractors must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM). In accordance with FAR RFO 22.13, and FAR RFO 52.222-35 Equal Opportunity for Veterans, contractors must have submitted the required annual VETS-4212, Federal Contractor Veterans Employment Report, with respect to the preceding fiscal year if the contractor was subject to the reporting requirements of 38 U.S.C.4212(d) for that fiscal year. The solicitation package should be available for download on or about October 1, 2026. No hard copies of the solicitation will be provided; and telephone requests or questions will NOT be accepted. Please email requests or questions to Liana.Holland@va.gov and ensure that the subject line reads 36C24526R0107 A&E IDIQ Question Request.

Non-DOD Users on DLA Teams ___________________________________________________________________ PREPROPOSAL CONFERENCE INFORMATION All interested vendors are welcome to join DLA Energy for a Preproposal Conference, which will be held virtually to discuss WESTPAC solicitation SPE602-26-R-0706. The Preproposal Conference will take place on April 16, 2026, and will provide information from the Procurement team. The conference is scheduled to begin at 09:30 AM U.S. Eastern Time (Local, Fort Belvoir) and end at 11:30 AM U.S. Eastern Time (Local, Fort Belvoir). Time will be set aside during the conference for additional questions, if needed. The agenda, presentation slides, and Microsoft Teams link will be posted on the www.sam.gov website on or before April 15, 2026. _________________________________________________________________________ DLA Energy anticipates hosting a Preproposal Conference to support an upcoming solicitation. The conference will be conducted virtually and will provide an overview of the solicitation, along with an opportunity for interested vendors to ask questions. The date and time of the Preproposal Conference are to be dermined (TBD). Additional details, including the agenda and vurtual meeting access information, will be posted on SAM.gov ata later date. _________________________________________________________________________ The WESTPAC Purchase Program covers the annual bulk petroleum requirements for the Western Pacific and Middle East Regions (F76, JA1 both neat and with additives, and JP5). Delivery modes will be by tanker, shallow draft tanker, barge, tanker truck, railcar, and pipeline. FOB destination tanker offers will not be accepted. These requirements may increase during the delivery period and be met by supplemental solicitations tied to this procurement. Details of the requirements for this procurement are as follows: Fuel, Naval Distillate (F76), NSN: 9140-00-273-2377, Purchase Program 1.1a Estimated Quantity: 207,670,000 U.S. Gallons (USG) Turbine Fuel, Aviation (JP5), NSN: 9130-00-273-2379, Purchase Program 1.1c Estimated Quantity: 137,574,000 U.S. Gallons (USG) Turbine Fuel, Aviation (JA1), NSN: 9130-00-753-5026, Purchase Program 1.1h Estimated Quantity: 266,390,000 U.S. Gallons (USG) of which some USG requires additives There will be no small business set asides on this procurement. The Contracting Officer intends to establish a phased selection process after the receipt of initial proposals. Under this approach, only offerors that meet the following minimum requirements in Phase 1 will advance in the evaluation process: � The Offeror is a refiner/manufacturer; or � The Offeror provides a Letter of Supply Commitment that meets the standards set forth in L3 Supplement: Evidence of Responsibility; or � The Offeror has successfully held a DLA Energy Bulk Petroleum Products contract within the past three (3) years. If an offeror fails to pass Phase 1, they will be notified and no negotiations will be conducted with no opportunity to revise their proposal.

title: Belgium – Soil-decontamination work – Sanering van met PFAS vervuilde grond op site BBEPP
description: Kandidaatstelling voor: Overeenkomst van werken voor de sanering van met PFAS vervuilde grond op een terrein van BBEPP. Bio Base Europe Pilot Plant heeft plannen om op een verworven stuk grond een waterzuiveringsinstallatie te bouwen. Het perceel is echter vervuild met PFAS, waardoor er eerst een sanering moet plaatsvinden. In kader van de grondoverdracht zijn de volgende documenten reeds opgesteld en conform verklaard door OVAM: • Oriënterend bodemonderzoek (OBO) • Beschrijvend bodemonderzoek (BBO) • Saneringskostenraming voor de procedure van versnelde overdracht In parallel met deze aanbesteding loopt er een project met een bodemdeskundige voor het opstellen van een bodemsaneringsproject (BSP). Om tijd te winnen is er gekozen om niet te wachten op dit BSP, maar dit bestek al te lanceren met vermoedelijke hoeveelheden. Bij aanvang van de werken zal een conform verklaard BSP beschikbaar zijn. Omvang van de werken omvat: • Grondwerken: Afgraven van 1800m³ met PFAS vervuilde grond. De concentraties vervuiling verschillen sterk: PFAS totaal tussen 3µg/kg DS en 2500µg/kg DS, met een gemiddelde rond 500µg/kg DS. Daarom is het aangewezen om de grond op te delen in verschillende partijen met gelijke graad van vervuiling, en deze partijen apart te behandelen met de best beschikbare techniek. • Grondwater: Afgraven dient te gebeuren tot maximaal 2m onder het maaiveld. Grondwaterstand bevindt zich op 3-4 meter onder het maaiveld, dus grondbemaling is niet nodig. • Grondreiniging: Afgegraven grond afvoeren en reinigen of storten • Nabehandeling: Aanvullen met propere grond en nivelleren Let op: opgegeven getallen zijn vermoedelijke hoeveelheden. Exacte cijfers zullen maar beschikbaar zijn na het opstellen van het BSP.

title: Netherlands – Teaching equipment – Leermiddelen VSO Stichting Koraal Groep
description: Stichting Koraal Groep is voornemens één raamovereenkomst te sluiten voor de levering, distributie en ondersteuning van fysieke en digitale leermiddelen en bijbehorende licenties voor haar scholen binnen het voortgezet speciaal onderwijs. De opdracht omvat onder meer het faciliteren van jaarbestellingen en nabestellingen, levering aan meerdere locaties, het beschikbaar stellen van een digitaal bestelportaal, licentiebeheer, retourafhandeling, ondersteuning van gebruikers en het verstrekken van managementinformatie. Het betreft circa 1.350 leerlingen. Dit aantal kan gedurende de looptijd van de raamovereenkomst fluctueren. De raamovereenkomst wordt gesloten met één opdrachtnemer voor een initiële periode van twee jaar, met de mogelijkheid tot tweemaal een verlenging van één jaar. De beoogde ingangsdatum is 1 januari 2027. De opdracht is niet verdeeld in percelen vanwege de inhoudelijke en operationele samenhang tussen levering, distributie en beheer van de leermiddelen. Stichting Koraal Groep behoudt zich het recht voor leermiddelen die de opdrachtnemer niet kan leveren bij derden af te nemen.

title: Netherlands – Teaching equipment – Leermiddelen SO Stichting Koraal Groep
description: Stichting Koraal Groep voert een Europese openbare aanbesteding uit voor de levering en dienstverlening rondom leermiddelen voor het speciaal basisonderwijs. De opdracht omvat het leveren, distribueren, beheren en – waar mogelijk – inzetten op hergebruik van fysieke en digitale leermiddelen, inclusief bijbehorende licenties. Tevens wordt van opdrachtnemer verwacht dat deze ondersteuning biedt bij het bestelproces, de logistiek, rapportage en het optimaliseren van leermiddelenlijsten. De dienstverlening dient aan te sluiten op de onderwijspraktijk van Koraal en kenmerkt zich door een sterk dienstverlenend karakter, waarbij continuïteit, gebruiksgemak voor interne bestellers en leverbetrouwbaarheid centraal staan. De opdracht wordt gegund op basis van de beste prijs-kwaliteitverhouding (EMVI).

title: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program
description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. � 121.702. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women�s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. title: Phytoremediation at the Eureka High Arctic Weather Station (HAWS)
description: The Eureka High Arctic Weather Station (HAWS) is situated in an isolated location on the north side of Slidre Fjord at the northwestern tip of Fosheim Peninsula, Ellesmere Island at approximately 80° N. The facility occupies a federal Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC) land reserve, #1021, spanning an area of 2.23 ha. Originally constructed primarily to conduct research in climatology and meteorology, the facility is owned and operated by Meteorological Service of Canada (MSC) and has been in operation since April 7th, 1947. The HAWS is located within in the Nunavut Settlement Area, part of the 350,000 km2 land claim granted to the Nunavut Inuit in 1993 but excluded from devolution. Although remote, the Eureka HAWS is a hub of activity for ECCC, the Department of National Defence (DND), the Polar Continental Shelf Project (PCSP), and the Polar Environment Atmospheric Research Lab (PEARL), to name a few. There are some areas of soil impacted with PHCs at the HAWS that cannot be excavated due to proximity to on-site infrastructure (e.g., buildings, pipelines) or due to risks associated with embankment stability and erosion. These areas present an opportunity for applying an alternative, low-carbon, green remedial approach. Phytoremediation is significantly less energy-intensive, more economical and requires minimal operation and maintenance than most conventional remedial methods which rely heavily on the use of heavy machinery. Although a proven technology, phytoremediation has not yet been applied as a remedial approach in the high arctic, success with phytoremediation at these latitudes is promising: (1) There is an abundance of plant species in the High Arctic and the HAWS area; (2) despite a short growing season, plants are exposed to 24-hour daylight for five months of the year, and (3) phytoremediation—enhanced with Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) seed treatments (PEPSystems®) to improve plant establishment and accelerate PHC degradation— has been applied at contaminated sites as far North as Norman Wells, in the Northwest Territories. The objective of this requirement is to obtain the services of a qualified contractor with recent experience in phytoremediation, ecological restoration, and contaminated site remediation to support the implementation, monitoring, and assessment of phytoremediation activities at the Eureka High Arctic Weather Station (HAWS). The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2029. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for A-Jetty Replacement
description: English Description DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – IE12347R – A-Jetty Replacement, CFB Esquimalt, British Columbia. Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary to construct the A Jetty including associated onshore infrastructure. This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. Requirements related to the Government of Canada's Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Materials in Federal Procurements will apply to this tender. Further details regarding any applicable requirements will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Project background The project is expected to be completed as a lump sum construction contract and may include unit rate prices and prime cost allowances. Work is to construct the A Jetty including associated onshore infrastructure. The new jetty will be constructed on piling and a combi wall (sheet pile system). The project scope also includes a tunnel inside A-Jetty. A two-storey substation building will also have to be built. Services required may include, but are not limited to, the following: Construction of A Jetty superstructure and associated infrastructure, including concrete works; Pile installation and pile caps; Backfilling; Civil works, site construction and services; Environmental remediation; Mechanical and electrical systems; Foreshore works; Project management and coordination; and Other various general contractor work. The River Class Destroyer (RCD) Extension to the A-Jetty may be added by change order. Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude (ROM) estimate for this Contract is $280 Million (Current Year $), which includes an estimated $20 million for the RCD Extension planned change order work. This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services,), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes GST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. Schedule DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around September 2026. The works shall reach substantial completion no later than 1681 calendar days following the notification of contract award and shall be completed no later than 90 calendar days after the substantial completion date. Site visit No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders may be invited to a site visit. Access to information Act Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act. Questions and clarifications Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System. DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer. In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System. Language of the Tender and the contract By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract. In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System. Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information:   the name of the joint venture, if applicable, the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable, the name of each member of the joint venture. Security Requirements During Construction The Contractor will be required to hold, at all times during the performance of the construction contract, at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) issued by Public Services and Procurement Canada's (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). In the case of a joint venture, all parties to the joint venture must hold at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS). DCC has issued an Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number IE12347R to allow contractors that do not hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) security clearance to initiate the sponsorship process prior to the launch of the tender phase. For information on the sponsorship process, consult the APN on MERX or visit https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. The Defense Health Agency may award Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreements (UF BPA) and the Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program Agreements (UF ADP) based on the UF decision. This process is described in the attached RFQ. P&T COMMITTEE MEETING: The following November 2026 drug classes/subclasses will be reviewed: a. Atopy - Topical Agents Anzupgo Eucrisa Opzelura Vtama Zoryve b. Lung Cancer - METEX14 Tabrecta Tepmetko The RFQ, including UF BPA and UF ADP appendices, are attached herein. The instructions, important deadlines, and points of contact are in document, RFQ HT9402-26-Q-9401. Pre-quotation teleconference is on August 12, 2026. Details are stated in Part 2.4. title: Nutrition Care Services; Forts Irwin, Leonard Wood, Riley, Stewart, and West Point
description: The solicitation number for the below-described requirement is HT940826RE017. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 722310, Food Service Contractors, which has a size standard of $47 million. The Defense Health Agency has a requirement for non-personal services providing qualified labor and management necessary to perform nutrition care food management, supervisory, technical, administrative, and clerical services that focus primarily on the following areas: dining facility management functions, therapeutic food preparation, patient tray assembly and delivery service, clinical training, facility sanitation, janitorial duties as it relates to the services being provided, and the associated logistics analysis and management functions in support of the Nutrition Care Divisions for five (5) Military Medical Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The following MTFs requiring the Nutrition Care Food Service support are: Weed Army Community Hospital (Fort Irwin, California), General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri), Irwin Army Community Hospital (Fort Riley, Kansas), Winn Army Community Hospital (Fort Stewart, Georgia), and Keller Army Community Hospital (West Point, New York). A transition period of 1 � 30 November 2026, base period of 1 December 2026 � 30 September 2027, and two (2) twelve-month option periods through 30 September 2029 are contemplated. The contract will be firm-fixed-price, with a set monthly price established per MTF. The Randolph Sheppard Act (RSA) applies to this requirement; therefore, priority will be given to any responsive State Licensing Agency (SLA) pursuant to the RSA. The priority established by the RSA applies to the award of contracts for the operation of cafeterias on Federal property. NOTE: The evaluation criteria will be the same for all offerors, including any responsible SLA. However, the solicitation will be issued on a full-and-open basis with a small business participation (eg, subcontracting) plan as one of the evaluation criteria for other-than-small businesses and non-SLAs. The solicitation is anticipated to be released on or about 10 September 2026, with an estimated closing date of 1 October 2026. The solicitation and all associated documents necessary for preparing a proposal will be posted on sam.gov. description: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide Local Guard Services to support the U.S. Mission in San Jose. The Government requires a secure environment to conduct their mission. The Contractor shall provide the organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the Performance Work Statement. The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, dependents, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). All contracted personnel, regardless of nationality, will be required to pass a background investigation conducted by the Contractor and a separate background investigation conducted by the U.S. Government to certify their suitability for employment under this contract. MTCCS II Ceiling Increase
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 5.203 to announce the Government's intent to increase the programmatic ordering ceiling of the Mission Training Complex Capability Support (MTCCS) II, Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC), by $129M on a noncompetitive basis. Services under this MATOC encompass non-personal operational, technical, administrative, and program management services supporting individual through collective MC training. The ceiling increase applies across the existing MTCCS II MATOC suite comprising the following base contracts: Base Contract Contractor W900KK-24-D-0003 Booz Allen Hamilton Inc W900KK-24-D-0004 CSA Global LLC W900KK-24-D-0005 General Dynamics Information Technology W900KK-24-D-0006 Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation W900KK-24-D-0007 Phoenix Logistics LLC W900KK-24-D-0008 Valiant Global Defense Services Inc. W900KK-24-D-0009 Applied Training Solutions LLC W900KK-24-D-0010 Core Government Services Corporation W900KK-24-D-0015 Veteran's First LLC W900KK-24-D-0014 Nemean Trideum Joint Venture LLC W900KK24D0012 Evocati Solutions JV W900KK24D0013 Liberty Business Solutions W900KK24D0020 Thalin W900KK24D0022 Gemini Technical Services The Army Contracting Command Aberdeen Proving Ground Orlando Division (ACC-APG-ORL) and the U.S Army Combined Arms Center have identified a critical need to increase the MTCCS II MATOC cumulative ceiling to ensure uninterrupted execution of the Army�s Mission Training Command (MTC) Program. The contemplated $129M ceiling increase is necessitated by environmental landscape changes and operational training demands, guaranteeing the continuation of vital Mission Command (MC) training delivered to units throughout the Army. Due to the ongoing operational tempo and specialized scope of work, no other contractors are currently positioned to assemble and mobilize the required administrative infrastructure, program management, and subject matter experts without creating an unacceptable mission lapse. Awarding the requirement to any sources other than the established MTCCS II contract holders would cause significant disruption of ongoing mission-critical training services. This is not a request for competitive quotes. The Government intends to award a sole source action to increase the MTCCS II contract ceilings under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as set forth in FAR 6.302-1 Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Interested firms that believe they possess the capabilities to satisfy the requirement may submit a written capability statement. Responding contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at sam.gov. All responses must be submitted no later than the Response Date and Time identified above. Email responses directly to the Contract Specialist, Guillermo Santiago-Sosa, at Guillermo.j.santiagososa.civ@army.mil. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) – Warehouse space
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately three (3) years, commencing on or about January 1, 2027, plus options to extend the lease for two (2) additional periods of one (1) year each; • approximately 280 - 550 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous warehouse or warehouse/office space and one (1) parking space; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. have two (2) separate, individual washrooms, and these washrooms will not form part of the Lessee’s usable space; 2. the proposed space must have all basic utilities, including telecommunications, water, sewer, gas and electricity (200 amps); 3. have electrical outlets installed throughout the leases premises, as mutually agreed to by the Lessee and Lessor; 4. be heated, or have the capability to be heated to a minimum of 20 degrees Celsius; 5. have a minimum unobstructed warehouse ceiling height of 3.05 metres (10’), measured from the top of the finished floor to the underside of the lowest obstruction of the ceiling, including HVAC, electrical, and sprinkler system; 6. have a loading facility with an overhead door, having a minimum size of 2.44 metres high x 2.44 metres wide (8’ x 8’); 7. have a man door for pedestrian access; 8. have, or have the capacity to install, an additional water supply for a janitor’s sink and/or drinking fountain; 9. combined warehouse/office space may be considered; 10. the dimensions of the proposed space must be compatible for efficient design and use; 11. the building systems must have the capacity to accommodate an occasional maximum occupancy of 30 people and a typical maximum occupancy of 20 people, in the space for a full day; 12. parking for approximately 14 vehicles must be available to the public within a one (1) block radius of the proposed space; 13. the physical characteristics of the lands and the building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; • the proposed space must be located within the following boundaries (the geographical boundaries include sites on either side of the roads): North: 144 Avenue NW/NE, South on Metis Trail NE, East on Country Hills Boulevard to Stoney Trail East: Stoney Trail, East on Township Road 250, South on Conrich Road/ 116 Street NE, West on 17 Avenue SE, South on Stoney Trail to Railway line/50 Avenue SE South: Railway line/50 Avenue SE to Deerfoot Trail, South on Deerfoot Trail, West on Glenmore Trail SW to Crowchild Trail SW West: Crowchild Trail SW/NW, North on Sarcee Trail NW to 144 Avenue NW In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. This map is to be used for presentation purposes only and is not a legal document • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

title: Surface Transportation Systems Engineering for Enabling Technologies Research and Development
description: This notice is issued by the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT), Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), Office of Acquisition and Grants Management. Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(3), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements) and FAR 6.103-3 (Industrial mobilization; engineering, developmental, or research capability; or expert services), the Government intends to negotiate and award a single-award, Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to: The MITRE Corporation 7525 Colshire Drive McLean, VA 22102 MITRE operates the Center for Advanced Aviation System Development (CAASD) Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC). Non-FAA government sponsors, including FHWA, are authorized to engage with and access the FFRDC's unique technical capabilities under Section V.C. of the CAASD FFRDC Sponsoring Agreement. FHWA requires non-personal systems engineering development, testing, and research services to support the Office of Safety and Operations Research & Development (HRSO) at the Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center (TFHRC) in McLean, VA. The effort, titled "Surface Transportation Systems Engineering for Enabling Technologies Research and Development," focuses on investigating and evaluating emerging technologies�including artificial intelligence (AI), edge computing, radio frequency (RF) spectrum and communications, network engineering, position, navigation, and timing (PNT), and cybersecurity�to improve safety and efficiency across surface transportation systems.

description: Amendment 003 : The purpose of this amendment is to extend the solicitation close date to 10/1/2026 [from 9/10/2026] Amendment 004: The purpose of this amendment is to update Attachment E - Questions and Answers Question Due date has been extended to 9/8/2026 at 9:00AM CST (Attachment was Posted to SAM.gov on 9/3/2026) Please reference the conformed copy (currently 80JSC026Q00060004) for all incorporated changes. ______________________________________________________________________________________ This notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Government reserves the right to make multiple awards from this RFQ. This notice is being issued as a Request for Quotations (RFQ) under solicitation number 80JSC026Q0006 for pilot chamber testing facilities capable of performing hypobaric Decompression Sickness (DCS) studies. The facilities are to perform three test days, collecting and recording data each day as they would for a research protocol. Please reference Attachment A - Statement of Work for mor details. The provisions and clauses in the RFQ are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Certification (FAC) Number 2026-01. The NAICS Code and Size Standard are 541714 and 1000 employees, respectively. The offeror must state in their offer their size status for this acquisition. All responsible sources may submit an offer which must be considered by the agency. The following clauses and provisions are incorporated; full text of the clauses and provisions may be accessed electronically at: FAR - FAR Overhaul - Part 52 | Acquisition.GOV NFS - https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/NFS.pdf Offerors must provide the information required by FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, September 2023, which is incorporated by reference. FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation -- Commercial Products and Commercial Services, November 2021. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the offer responsible, whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors are in descending order of importance and must be used to evaluate offers: technical acceptability, past performance, and price. FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, (November 2023). All offerors shall reference the additional submission requirements in Attachment D - Additional Submission Criteria dated 07/15/2026. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf This posting, in addition to any attached documents, will be available on www.Sam.gov. Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their own copy of this combination synopsis/solicitation and amendments (if any). Prospective offerors are encouraged to notify this office of their intent to submit an offer. All contractual and technical questions must be submitted electronically via email to Tracy.L.Quintanilla@nasa.gov, and Katelyn.R.Jaime@nasa.gov, not later than September 8, 2026, 9:00 a.m. Central Time. Telephone questions will not be accepted. Responses to this combined synopsis/solicitation must be received via e-mail to Tracy.L.Quintanilla@nasa.gov, and Katelyn.R.Jaime@nasa.gov, no later than 1:00 p.m. Central Time, on October 1, 2026. The Government is not responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of documents submitted using electronic means, including the missing of any established deadlines. Failure to submit a complete electronic quote by the due date and time specified for this RFQ must result in the proposal being considered late and must be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1(c)(2).

title: Performance Oriented Construction Activity (POCA) for Nashville District
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE BEING RELEASED PURSUANT TO REVOLUTIONARY FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION OVERHAUL (RFO) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. SCOPE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Nashville District anticipates a requirement for two (2) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Firm-Fixed, Performance Oriented Construction Activity (POCA), for the Nashville District�s East Region and West Region. Each region�s POCA contract has an anticipated capacity of $2 million for the base year and $2 million for each of the subsequent 4 option years. Task orders issued under the subject POCAs are not anticipated to exceed the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT). SEE ATTACHED DOCUMENT FOR MORE DETAILED INFORMATION. SURVEY: The Government is issuing this notice to determine a competitive basis. This is not a solicitation and the items listed herein are subject to change or elimination from the requirement. Only contractors capable of supplying this type of procurement should respond to this survey. Respondents interested in providing a response to this RFI/Sources Sought should submit information which clearly describes the following: Name of your firm, address, points of contact with telephone numbers and e-mail addresses and CAGE code and or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Are you a Small Business classified under the 238990 NAICS code? If so do you fall into a sub-category (e.g. HubZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc)? Are you able to perform the type of construction activities described above and do you have the capacity to perform the work? Please provide a Statement of Capability stating your skills, experience, and knowledge required to perform the specified type of work. Include a statement detailing any special qualifications and certifications applicable to the scope of this project. Which region(s) does your business anticipate submitting a proposal for? Do you currently have the ability to operate at the more remote sites listed (e.g., Martins Fork Dam, Laurel River Dam, and Dale Hollow Dam), or do you have pre-established vendor/subcontractor relationships in those areas? Which pricing approach does your firm strongly prefer for task orders issued under this contract? Approach A: Pre-Established Base Unit Rates with Geographic/Location Multipliers (e.g., fixed master line-item rates / unit price schedules established at the base IDIQ level, adjusted by pre-set coefficient multipliers based on distance/location of each specific dam/lake project). Approach B: Competitive / Individual Pricing per Task Order (e.g., independent lump-sum or line-item quotes submitted for each individual task order requirement at the time of issuance).Approach C: Hybrid Approach (e.g., pre-established hourly labor/equipment rates combined with negotiated task-specific material costs). Do you have any feedback or recommendations regarding the proposed scope, the East/West regional division, or task order execution under this planned POCA IDIQ?Do you have experience working with Unified Facilities Guide Specifications and/or preparing project specifications in SpecsIntact for the task orders? Please describe any recent contracts or experience within the previous 36 months that are similar to the requirements described above. If this requirement is advertised, do you anticipate submitting a proposal? RESPONSES: Please submit your response no later than 1:00 PM Central Standard Time on Thursday, October 01, 2026 via email to Alison Abernathy and Jori Jackson- alison.t.abernathy@usce.army.mil and jori.l.jackson@usace.army.mil

title: 3587 Dredge CURRITUCK Replacement Notice of Intent to Sole Source
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT Notice ID: PANNAD-26-P-0000 032679 Department/Agency: USACE Philadelphia District Product Service Code (PSC): 1955 Dredges NAICS Code: 336611 � Ship Building and Repairing Introduction and Background This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with RFO 5.101. This Notice does NOT constitute a request for competitive proposals, bids or quotes. The USACE Philadelphia District intends to award a contract on a noncompetitive basis under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii) ("Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements"). Intended Awardee: Conrad Shipyard, LLC UEI: W1JVE3BNA7P1 CAGE Code: 5GE25 Address: 1501 Front Street, Morgan City, Louisiana 70380, United States 2. Authority The proposed procurement is justified under the authority of 10 USC �3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii). This authority is applicable because the required special purpose dredge, as described as the agency requirement below, must be procured from Conrad Shipyard, LLC (Conrad) to avoid unacceptable delays in fulfilling USACE�s requirement. Delays will be avoided due to Conrad�s previous experience producing this highly specialized dredge. 3. Description of Agency Requirement The Government requires the design, build, test, and delivery of one new special purpose, split-hull, trailing suction shallow draft hopper dredge to replace the Dredge Currituck. The following are the agency requirements for this procurement. Schedule, Operational, and Regulatory Requirements: Schedule Requirements: The contractor will be able to start vessel construction within 12 � 16 weeks following contract award with design submittals for ABS/USCG approval coordinated to support the construction sequence. The vessel construction will be able to be completed within a 16-month duration period. Operational Requirements: The shallow draft dredge will be designed for working in shallow draft ocean bar channels along the Atlantic Coast of the United States from Maine to Texas year-round. Hull: The shallow draft dredge will have a split hull that utilizes a water hydraulic actuation and latching system. Draft: The shallow draft dredge will be designed with a draft of 9 feet, 5 inches, fully loaded and a draft of 4 feet, 3 inches with the hopper empty. Dredging Depth: The shallow draft dredge will be designed to dredge to a depth of 20 feet. Speed: The shallow draft dredge will have a minimum speed of 7 knots with the hopper fully loaded and a minimum speed of 10 knots with the hopper empty. Capacity: The shallow draft dredge will have a hopper capacity of 518 cubic yards at 1.915 S.G. Length: The shallow draft dredge will have a length of 156 feet. Beam: The shallow draft dredge will have a beam of 35 feet. Propulsion: The shallow draft dredge will be self-propelled and utilize Azimuthing thrusters. Functional Requirements: The shallow draft dredge will be designed as a day boat to support 12-hour operations for a period of 7 days. The design will allow sufficient tankage and storage space for consumables to support combined dredging and free sailing operations for 7 days. These requirements will allow the shallow draft to respond to missions effectively and efficiently along the East Coast. Warranty: A one-year warranty period is required following final acceptance and delivery. Regulatory Requirements: American Bureau of Shipping (ABS): The new shallow draft dredge will be ABS classed and will also be assigned a Load Line Certificate issued by ABS. The ABS classification will be Maltese Cross A1, Maltese Cross AMS, Domestic Service, with a Vessel Description of Hopper Dredger. U.S. Coast Guard (USCG): A new shallow draft dredge will be USCG certificated under the requirements of 46 CFR Subchapter I. 4. Justification for Sole Source The USACE Philadelphia District has determined that Conrad Shipyard, LLC (�Conrad�) is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the agency requirements without causing unacceptable delays. Specifically, this requirement is a follow-on contract of the USACE DREDGE MURDEN, which was designed, constructed, and delivered by Conrad in 2012. As such, Conrad has comprehensive knowledge of the critical and complex components of the DREDGE MURDEN, including ownership of elements of the technical design package. As such, through design and construction efficiencies, Conrad can ensure swift delivery of the vessel thereby avoiding unacceptable delays in fulfilling USACE�s requirements. Award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency requirements and lead to unacceptable delays to the CURRITUCK�s mission. 5. Market Research Market research confirmed that no other contractor can adhere to the agency requirement without presenting unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency requirements. This was confirmed through a Source Sought Notification issued on 11AUG2026 that was published for 15 days. 6. Conclusion To avoid unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency requirements, the only viable path is to procure the highly specialized dredge from Conrad Shipyard, LLC. Therefore, a sole-source justification pursuant to RFO 6.103-1 is appropriate and necessary to avoid unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency requirement described herein.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ERDC Fellowship Program Administration and Research Support Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research Notice ID: PANERD-26-P-0000-027000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541715 � R&D in Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences Product Service Code (PSC): R425 � Support�Professional: Engineering/Technical Size Standard: 1,000 Employees 1. Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), is conducting market research to identify capable small businesses and other-than-small businesses that can establish and administer an ERDC Fellowship Program. This notice is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, commitment by the Government, or promise to issue a solicitation or make an award. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Responses will help the Government assess the availability, capability, capacity, and socioeconomic status of potential sources and inform acquisition planning, including any small-business strategy. The Government has not made a determination regarding set-aside status, acquisition approach, contract type, evaluation criteria, or award decision. 2. Requirement Overview ERDC seeks a contractor capable of serving as an integrator between scientifically accredited universities and ERDC laboratories to establish and administer a fellowship program. The program is intended to enable scientists, engineers, and postsecondary students to perform independent research that addresses ERDC-defined problems and supports science and technology objectives with potential civil and military applications. The anticipated requirement is for a single-award indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract under which ERDC laboratories would issue and fund individual task orders for laboratory-specific research efforts. The Performance Work Statement (PWS) identifies the following ERDC laboratories as anticipated users: Construction Engineering Research Laboratory (CERL), Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory (CHL), Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (CRREL), Environmental Laboratory (EL), Geospatial Research Laboratory (GRL), Geotechnical Structures Laboratory (GSL), and Information Technology Laboratory (ITL). The current PWS contemplates a five-year ordering period consisting of one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. 3. Scope of Needed Capabilities The Government seeks information from firms capable of providing end-to-end fellowship program administration, including the ability to: Recruit, screen, and manage Fellows in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and related disciplines; Administer fellowship appointments and support research opportunities aligned with ERDC task-order requirements; Pay Fellows and manage administrative logistics, performance, records, and program operations; Support fellowship opportunities across the following categories: Postdoctoral Fellows; Senior Fellows; Journeyman Fellows; Short-Term Fellows; and Summer Student Experience participants. The PWS describes fellow categories and eligibility requirements that span postdoctoral researchers, established investigators, degree holders, postsecondary students, faculty, and summer research participants. Support research opportunities in the following technical focus areas: Water Resources and Environmental Security; Dynamic and Extreme Mechanics of Structures and Geomaterials; Cold Engineering and Science; Integrative Geospatial Analytics and Decision Science; Resilient Infrastructure and Installations; and Digital Engineering and Prototyping. Manage task-order-specific travel requirements; Support onsite collaboration at Government facilities when required, including compliance with applicable facility safety, environmental, security, and operational requirements; Support background-check, access, and training requirements as applicable to individual task orders; Manage intellectual-property-related administrative requirements, including execution and administration of applicable fellow intellectual-property agreements; and Provide program-management support, including kickoff meetings, monthly progress meetings, periodic progress reporting, and quality-management processes. The Government may provide office space, communications connectivity, and information technology equipment when required and available. Task-order requirements will identify specific Government-furnished property, locations, access requirements, deliverables, and travel needs. 4. Performance Considerations Respondents should address their ability to support a performance-based requirement in which contractor performance may be assessed on quality, timeliness of deliverables, customer satisfaction, and timeliness and accuracy of invoices and reports. The PWS anticipates contractor quality-management processes and Government surveillance of performance outcomes. The anticipated requirement may include, as applicable to task-order performance: Virtual and onsite collaboration; Government-facility access requirements; Antiterrorism, operational security, information-assurance, and related training requirements; Suitability or background-screening requirements for Fellows; No anticipated access to or exchange of Controlled Unclassified Information under the current PWS; and Quarterly progress reports and task-order-specific deliverables. 5. Requested Capability Statement Interested firms should submit a concise capability statement of no more than [5] pages, excluding cover page and attachments. Marketing materials alone are not sufficient. Responses should include: Company Information Legal business name; Unique Entity Identifier; Physical address; Primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address; Business size under the NAICS code identified in this notice; Socioeconomic status, if applicable, including: Small Business; Small Disadvantaged Business; 8(a) Business Development Program participant; HUBZone Small Business; Woman-Owned Small Business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business; and/or Veteran-Owned Small Business; Identification of any existing Government contract vehicles that may be relevant to this requirement. Relevant Experience Provide up to three examples of comparable work performed within the past five years. For each example, include: Customer name and organization; Contract or agreement number, if releasable; Period of performance; Total value; Description of work performed; Number and types of participants managed; Relevant technical disciplines or research areas supported; Experience coordinating with universities, laboratories, research institutions, or Government organizations; Experience with Fellow, intern, student, scholar, research-associate, or similar appointment programs; and Customer point of contact, if available and authorized for release. Technical and Management Capability Describe the firm�s capability to: Recruit and maintain access to a diverse, qualified pipeline of candidates; Validate education, credentials, and eligibility requirements; Manage Fellow onboarding, payments, performance, records, and offboarding; Manage concurrent task orders with different laboratory requirements, funding sources, schedules, and technical focus areas; Support onsite and remote performance; Manage travel at the task-order level; Support intellectual-property agreement administration and associated recordkeeping; Implement quality-control procedures and measure performance outcomes; Meet reporting requirements and provide accurate, timely invoices; and Manage applicable personnel-screening, facility-access, and training requirements. title: Engineering, Technical, and Programmatic Support Services for Weapon Systems Development Division (Code JXP)
description: This is a Sources Sought notice issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC Crane) in support of the Weapon Systems Development Division (Code JXP). This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the Department of War (DoW) to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the respondents expense. NSWC Crane Code JXP serves as the Navys engineering agent and full life-cycle support facility, providing technical leadership in the areas of Small Arms, Small Arms Ammunition, Pyrotechnics, Demolitions, Asymmetric Initiation Systems, and Unmanned/Counter-Unmanned Systems (UxS/C-UxS). The Government requires non-personal Level of Effort (LOE) engineering, technical, programmatic, management, test and evaluation, logistics, and in-service support services. The operational environment requires support across indoor/outdoor firing ranges, explosive test facilities, and laboratories. Performance requires access to classified information up to the SECRET level and requires specialized personnel certifications (e.g., Level I/II NDT Radiographers, CDL HAZMAT drivers, and Cyber Security Workforce [CSWF] credentials). The Government intends to utilize the SeaPort-NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC) vehicle for this procurement. The anticipated contract type is Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort Task Order. The primary objectives of this Sources Sought are to: 1. Determine Industrial Base Capabilities: Assess the capabilities of Small Business and Large Business SeaPort-NxG prime contractors to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy (e.g., 100% Small Business Set-Aside vs. Unrestricted Competition). 2. Optimize for Executive Order (EO) 14402: Solicit specific industry feedback to identify SOW tasking that is sufficiently mature, predictable, and deliverable-based to be executed as Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) rather than CPFF. 3. Enhance Performance-Based Acquisition (PBA): Solicit industry recommendations on the draft Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) to establish objective, measurable Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs) and effective incentive/disincentive structures.

title: The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times)
description: Description This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or questions. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain knowledge and information for project planning purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The NIH seeks information on technologies and capabilities to further the objectives of the Data COUNTS program. The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times) effort is built on collaboration between patients and advocates, government, health systems, technology companies, and the private sector. The Data COUNTS program enables the NIH�s Real-World Data initiative and will provide high quality, standardized data that is provenanced and available through approved access to the research community. The contemplated capability will initially perform requested and approved extraction from Healthcare Partner EMR systems and should be modular and extensible to other authorized source systems such as laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, picture archiving and communication systems, vendor-neutral archives, and specialty systems. The Data COUNTS program requires that source data, and source provenance metadata, permissions, and source ontology fields will be preserved without modification or loss. This program will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Technical Requirements of Interest: Address availability and technologies that enable the following features: A durable, Healthcare Partner Leave Behind Technology capability that remains at the Healthcare Partner site after contract completion and can be operated by trained staff without ongoing involvement. The technology should be available and free for use by Healthcare Partners while in the Data COUNTS program. Describe any installation and configuration documentation, operational runbooks, site-controlled credential-transfer procedures, documented dependencies, major-release update procedures, and training that enable independent site operations. Deep query for approved extraction from Healthcare Partner electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other authorized source systems. Capture timestamps and provenance for all data at extraction and maintain an immutable provenance chain. The architecture consumes a machine-readable, version-controlled, authorized, and approved Data Request Specification defining cohort logic, requested source systems, data domains and fields, date range, full or incremental extraction mode, refresh cadence, and applicable authorization and permission rules. Describe how the solution validates data availability against the specification, identifies unavailable or ambiguous fields, avoids silent substitutions, associates the request identifier with each batch and output, and supports reproducible reruns when source data have not changed. An initial automated data quality check validating completeness, uniqueness, data types, date sequencing, and records-per-patient. All anomalies must be reported before any permitted corrections are applied. Sourced data will not be modified De-identification per 45 CFR �164.514(b): remove all 18 direct identifiers; document a consistent de-identification pathway; and apply a per-patient date-shifting specification that preserves temporal order. Privacy Preserving Record Linkage (PPRL) tokenization capabilities for cross-site linkage using an approved, on-premises within the institutional trust boundary PPRL platform that generates consistent, irreversible patient tokens. Describe validation and Healthcare Partner approval before the first live transmission. Describe how token consistency is achieved across independently deployed, site-local PPRL instances, without introducing a shared trust boundary outside the Healthcare Partner site. Describe how the solution preserves all source provenance metadata, permissions information, and ontology fields (e.g. SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, RxNorm, UCUM, etc.) without modification or loss, excluding authorized de-identification transformations performed under Section 4. The DSP will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Metadata must be additive, clearly identified, and each output value must be traceable to the source and authorized transformation. Describe how the solution consumes authoritative eligibility supplied by the Healthcare Partner and applies it before transmission; records the governing authorization or permission version for each dataset; distinguish cohort exclusions from permission exclusions; and apply revocations so that revoked records are absent from all subsequent refreshes. Describe how the solution generates full and incremental extracts; maintains stable patient tokens; creates unique snapshot and refresh IDs; supports idempotent reruns; identifies added, updated, deleted, merged, unmerged, corrected, and late-arriving records to the appropriate refresh cycle. Workflow Integrity & Processing Audit: maintain audit records for each stage; timestamp, stage ID, batch ID, record counts, outcome, and reconciliation status. Failed reconciliations or incomplete processing stages must halt transmission until resolved or authorized for reprocessing. Security Posture: Describe the ability to attest to HIPAA Security Rule compliance as a Business Associate; Security Audit Logging to generate SIEM-compatible security logs for authentication, administrative actions, configuration changes, and security events. Record timestamp, user/service account, action, resource, and outcome. Security logs must be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and logging must be continuous. Defense-in-Depth Encryption: TLS 1.3 where supported; TLS 1.2 minimum for all data in transit,; application-level encryption of output files and VM-level encryption. Attack Surface Minimization with no unnecessary ports, services, or network listeners by default. The only authorized external connection is the outbound TLS path to the Data COUNT Program Also see Section 1 regarding on-site operation of Leave Behind Technology; this section addresses the boundary for identifiable data processing. Describe how identifiable processing is confined to the Healthcare Partner�s VM and institutional trust boundary; only de-identified, tokenized output is transmitted for the Data COUNTS program; access is integrated with Healthcare Partner identity and access controls and is site-managed and logged; and the deployed solution does not include or permit contractor credentials, contractor remote-access pathways, or contractor remote-management capabilities. Describe supported performance at baseline, 2X, and 5X expected workloads and identify assumed data volumes, throughput, processing time, and Healthcare Partner CPU, memory, storage, network and staffing requirements. Describe how the solution can reliably package, transmit, reconcile, and retry deliveries to the TDB, including package, schema versioning, and error resolution. Business Information Requested Please provide information on the following: Details on which capabilities are able to be met Clarification on which features are commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), and which features would be considered minor modifications, and which features would be considered custom development features Billing model and pricing structure and any additional features and their subsequent costs Experience with successful implementation capabilities and list of healthcare partners Experience of similar work with Federal Government agencies Experience of similar work with industries or non-profit organizations Business size and status Response Format: Responses must be submitted by October 1, 2026, 3:00 Eastern Standard Time to DataCounts@nih.gov with the subject line Company Name RFI Response. Responses must be submitted in PDF o
