title: SOURCES SOUGHT: ERDC Fellowship Program Administration and Research Support
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ERDC Fellowship Program Administration and Research Support Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research Notice ID: PANERD-26-P-0000-027000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541715 � R&D in Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences Product Service Code (PSC): R425 � Support�Professional: Engineering/Technical Size Standard: 1,000 Employees 1. Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), is conducting market research to identify capable small businesses and other-than-small businesses that can establish and administer an ERDC Fellowship Program. This notice is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, commitment by the Government, or promise to issue a solicitation or make an award. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Responses will help the Government assess the availability, capability, capacity, and socioeconomic status of potential sources and inform acquisition planning, including any small-business strategy. The Government has not made a determination regarding set-aside status, acquisition approach, contract type, evaluation criteria, or award decision. 2. Requirement Overview ERDC seeks a contractor capable of serving as an integrator between scientifically accredited universities and ERDC laboratories to establish and administer a fellowship program. The program is intended to enable scientists, engineers, and postsecondary students to perform independent research that addresses ERDC-defined problems and supports science and technology objectives with potential civil and military applications. The anticipated requirement is for a single-award indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract under which ERDC laboratories would issue and fund individual task orders for laboratory-specific research efforts. The Performance Work Statement (PWS) identifies the following ERDC laboratories as anticipated users: Construction Engineering Research Laboratory (CERL), Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory (CHL), Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (CRREL), Environmental Laboratory (EL), Geospatial Research Laboratory (GRL), Geotechnical Structures Laboratory (GSL), and Information Technology Laboratory (ITL). The current PWS contemplates a five-year ordering period consisting of one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. 3. Scope of Needed Capabilities The Government seeks information from firms capable of providing end-to-end fellowship program administration, including the ability to: a. Recruit, screen, and manage Fellows in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and related disciplines; b. Administer fellowship appointments and support research opportunities aligned with ERDC task-order requirements; c. Pay Fellows and manage administrative logistics, performance, records, and program operations; d. Support fellowship opportunities across the following categories: Postdoctoral Fellows; Senior Fellows; Journeyman Fellows; Short-Term Fellows; and Summer Student Experience participants. The PWS describes fellow categories and eligibility requirements that span postdoctoral researchers, established investigators, degree holders, postsecondary students, faculty, and summer research participants. e. Support research opportunities in the following technical focus areas: Water Resources and Environmental Security; Dynamic and Extreme Mechanics of Structures and Geomaterials; Cold Engineering and Science; Integrative Geospatial Analytics and Decision Science; Resilient Infrastructure and Installations; and Digital Engineering and Prototyping. f. Manage task-order-specific travel requirements; g. Support onsite collaboration at Government facilities when required, including compliance with applicable facility safety, environmental, security, and operational requirements; h. Support background-check, access, and training requirements as applicable to individual task orders; i. Manage intellectual-property-related administrative requirements, including execution and administration of applicable fellow intellectual-property agreements; and j. Provide program-management support, including kickoff meetings, monthly progress meetings, periodic progress reporting, and quality-management processes. The Government may provide office space, communications connectivity, and information technology equipment when required and available. Task-order requirements will identify specific Government-furnished property, locations, access requirements, deliverables, and travel needs. 4. Performance Considerations Respondents should address their ability to support a performance-based requirement in which contractor performance may be assessed on quality, timeliness of deliverables, customer satisfaction, and timeliness and accuracy of invoices and reports. The PWS anticipates contractor quality-management processes and Government surveillance of performance outcomes. The anticipated requirement may include, as applicable to task-order performance: Virtual and onsite collaboration; Government-facility access requirements; Antiterrorism, operational security, information-assurance, and related training requirements; Suitability or background-screening requirements for Fellows; No anticipated access to or exchange of Controlled Unclassified Information under the current PWS; and Quarterly progress reports and task-order-specific deliverables. 5. Requested Capability Statement Interested firms should submit a concise capability statement of no more than [5] pages, excluding cover page and attachments. Marketing materials alone are not sufficient. Responses should include: a. Company Information 1. Legal business name; 2. Unique Entity Identifier; 3. Physical address; 4. Primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address; 5. Business size under the NAICS code identified in this notice; 6. Socioeconomic status, if applicable, including: Small Business; Small Disadvantaged Business; 8(a) Business Development Program participant; HUBZone Small Business; Woman-Owned Small Business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business; and/or Veteran-Owned Small Business; 7. Identification of any existing Government contract vehicles that may be relevant to this requirement. b. Relevant Experience Provide up to three examples of comparable work performed within the past five years. For each example, include: 1. Customer name and organization; 2. Contract or agreement number, if releasable; 3. Period of performance; 4. Total value; 5. Description of work performed; 6. Number and types of participants managed; 7. Relevant technical disciplines or research areas supported; 8. Experience coordinating with universities, laboratories, research institutions, or Government organizations; 9. Experience with Fellow, intern, student, scholar, research-associate, or similar appointment programs; and 10. Customer point of contact, if available and authorized for release. c. Technical and Management Capability Describe the firm�s capability to: 1. Recruit and maintain access to a diverse, qualified pipeline of candidates; 2. Validate education, credentials, and eligibility requirements; 3. Manage Fellow onboarding, payments, performance, records, and offboarding; 4. Manage concurrent task orders with different laboratory requirements, funding sources, schedules, and technical focus areas; 5. Support onsite and remote performance; 6. Manage travel at the task-order level; 7. Support intellectual-property agreement administration and associated recordkeeping; 8. Implement quality-control procedures and measure performance outcomes; 9. Meet reporting requirements and provide accurate, timely invoices; and 10. title: REPAIR OF THE RECEIVER TRANSMITTERS, APPLICABLE TO THE LIGHTWEIGHT AIRBORNE RECOVERY SYSTEM (LARS).
description: This requirement is for the repair services of three (3) Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) supporting the Lightweight Airborne Recovery System (LARS) utilized on A-10, HC-130J, HH-60G, and HC-130P/N aircraft: LARS R/T (P/N 282650-1, NSN 5820-01-561-9642) [HC-130(H)N and A-10] LARS R/T (P/N 282650-2, NSN 5820-01-662-1038SO) [HH-60G] LARS R/T (P/N 282650-3, NSN 5821-01-661-5866SO) [HC-130J] The LARS R/T is a critical search and rescue component containing a fully synthesized UHF receiver/transmitter that provides voice communication, range, and direction measurements to interrogate survival radios of downed airmen. The period of performance for the contract/order will be one base year with (4) One year ordering periods and extend one year beyond the date of the final order or will end on the last day of the contract. Cubic Secure Communications, LLC. is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of these Antennas.They own the technical data package, all the data rights, and performance specifications that cannot be acquired in the commercial market sector. A complete technical data package is required to repair the LARS. The Government lacks repair data and does not possess any commercial product sheets, test data, qualification data, support manuals or related data that defines the performance and manufacturing characteristics of the LARS, precluding organic and competitive repair. The repair requirement is military unique as these components are only used on military platforms. Cubic Secure Communications, LLC. is the only known source that has the facility, expertise, tooling and parts to repair these components in a timely manner. Cubic responded in an email on 30 September 2025 that they are not interested in selling data to the Government. Cubic is the only qualified source capable of repairing the LARS due to their proprietary rights. The type of contract anticipated is a Firm Fixed Price / Indefinite Delivery Requirements Contract in accordance with RFO 16.202 and 16.503. This repair contract meets the definition of a service contract in accordance with RFO 37.001 therefore a performance based work statement (PWS) will be utilized to the maximum extent possible along with a Quality Assessment Surveillance Plan (QASP) in which a Contracting Officer Representative (COR) will be assigned. There will be no paper copies of this requirement mailed. No telephone or fax requests will be honored. The approximate response date is 1 October 2026. Late responses will not be accepted. The anticipated award date is 10 December 2026. Questions should be emailed to Kyra Harris at kyra.harris@us.af.mil and Leigh Ann Taylor at leigh.ann.taylor@us.af.mil. no later than 17 September 2026, 4:00 pm EDT. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency.

title: Vocational Training Programs
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part RFO FAR part 12.202. This announcement constitutes the solicitation only. Quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Mission Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington currently intends to award a contract for Education and Vocational Training for prisoners confined at the Northwestern Joint Regional Correctional Facility (NWJRCF). The NWJRCF prison inmate population is located at 20000 Alder Rd, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, WA 98433. The contractor shall provide instructors and state approved curriculum for a Vocational Training Program to provide prisoners with the knowledge and skills for future employment, preparation for certification, degrees, and licensure. The NWJRCF is a medium security correctional facility which houses military prisoners with sentences up to 10 years. The mission of the NWJRCF is to provide custody/control, education, and vocational opportunities as well as behavioral/mental health programs to prisoners to assist their transition back into the civilian community or return to duty. The NWJRCF houses prisoners in the military correctional system. Prisoners who demonstrate good behavior, desire to learn, who qualify after screening, and with enough time remaining in their sentences may be enrolled in vocational education programs. The prisoners work toward good conduct time and are kept gainfully employed by learning new skills that in turn prepare them for work upon release. All duties shall be performed in accordance with standards and methods generally accepted within industry and in compliance with all Federal and State policies and regulations. The U.S. Government highly encourages all interested businesses (large and small) to respond to this RFQ.

title: Vocational Training Programs
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part RFO FAR part 12.202. This announcement constitutes the solicitation only. Quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Mission Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington currently intends to award a contract for Education and Vocational Training for prisoners confined at the Northwestern Joint Regional Correctional Facility (NWJRCF). The NWJRCF prison inmate population is located at 20000 Alder Rd, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, WA 98433. The contractor shall provide instructors and state approved curriculum for a Vocational Training Program to provide prisoners with the knowledge and skills for future employment, preparation for certification, degrees, and licensure. The NWJRCF is a medium security correctional facility which houses military prisoners with sentences up to 10 years. The mission of the NWJRCF is to provide custody/control, education, and vocational opportunities as well as behavioral/mental health programs to prisoners to assist their transition back into the civilian community or return to duty. The NWJRCF houses prisoners in the military correctional system. Prisoners who demonstrate good behavior, desire to learn, who qualify after screening, and with enough time remaining in their sentences may be enrolled in vocational education programs. The prisoners work toward good conduct time and are kept gainfully employed by learning new skills that in turn prepare them for work upon release. All duties shall be performed in accordance with standards and methods generally accepted within industry and in compliance with all Federal and State policies and regulations. The U.S. Government highly encourages all interested businesses (large and small) to respond to this RFQ.

J. Hughes Technical Center (WJHTC) , Egg Harbor Township, NJ NAICS Code: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction PSC: Y1DB, Construction of Laboratories and Clinics Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $25,000,000 and $75,000,000 Anticipated Solicitation Issuance Date: April 2027 Estimated duration of the project: 1,095 Calendar Days Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Design-Build (DB) Contract Anticipated Acquisition Method: RFO 36.101-2 Two-Phase Design Build Selection Procedures and RFO Part 15 Negotiated Procurement using �Best Value� tradeoff process High Level Project Summary: The Transportation Security Laboratory (TSL) is a federal laboratory aligned under the Science and Technology Directorate of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The Transportation Security Laboratory (TSL) campus is located along the eastern boundary of the William F. Hughes FAA Technical Center at the Atlantic City International Airport. TSL is responsible for researching, developing, engineering, testing and evaluating solutions to detect and mitigate the threat of Improvised Explosive Devices and weapons used against our Nation�s transportation systems. The project entails construction of a Detection Sciences, Testing and Applied Research Center (DSTARC) and the associated Facility for Energetic Materials Research (FEMR) building, including supporting infrastructure (hereafter referred to as the �DSTAR Project�). The project entails the construction of an approx. 40,000 SF Detection Sciences Testing and Applied Research Center (DSTARC) laboratory, an approximately 6,000 SF Facility for Energetic Materials Research (FEMR) laboratory, and ancillary site improvements to support these buildings. The combined buildings will enable TSL to perform trace material characterization and develop testing methods and protocols to detect and mitigate the threat of improvised explosive devices. The multi-story DSTARC will be composed of pile foundations, steel framing and brick veneer, painted metal panel exterior with standing seam metal roofing. Interior construction will consist of reinforced concrete masonry walls, metal stud, gypsum board walls and operable / movable partition walls Detection Sciences Testing and Applied Research Center laboratory building will include modern office space, conference rooms, laboratory areas, chemical and hazardous waste storage aeras, sensitive compartmented information facility areas, blast hardened features, loading dock, etc. Classified work areas shall be designed in accordance with DHS requirements. Specific laboratories within the DSTAR complex shall be blast hardened to withstand small quantity material detonations of up to 5 grams. The approximate 6,000 SF Facility for Energetic Materials Research laboratory will include laboratories, office space, and a control room dedicated to energetic materials synthesis and full-scale safety testing of these materials. The Energetic Material Synthesis Laboratory shall be capable of withstanding the detonation of up to two kilograms of explosives without damage to other laboratories or buildings, or serious injury to personnel outside of the Energetic Material Synthesis Laboratory. Other laboratories within the DSTAR complex shall be blast hardened to withstand small quantity material detonations of up to 5 grams. The project also includes related infrastructure such as parking areas, roads, utilities, and site improvements. Roads and parking will integrate with existing infrastructure in a manner that facilities foot and vehicle traffic in and around the TSL campus. Minimum Technical Requirements and Critical Features of Work: The DSTAR buildings shall have the capability to securely and efficiently exchange documents with classifications levels up to Top-Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) documents and data with authorized individuals and organizations in Secret Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCIF) and Top Secret Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS-SCI) Areas. The DSTARC building will become the main IT hub for the TSL campus. All building controls, security and fire systems, mechanical and information technology systems shall be able to fully integrate with existing TSL infrastructure. All fire system installations and modifications shall be in accordance with the Transportation Security Laboratory Campus-Wide Fire Alarm System Planning Considerations white paper written by the FAA WJHTC Project Engineering and Construction Office in January 2010. The Chemistry Complex shall have environmental controls and systems independent of HVAC systems in the rest of the building to prevent or mitigate contamination of these spaces. The HVAC system for the Chemistry Complex shall be able to meet temperature, humidity, and relative pressure requirements and ASHRAE 55 standards while fume hoods are operating. The DSTAR buildings require enhanced commissioning upon completion to validate energy performance. Other Known Challenges: The TSL campus is located within the federally secured FAA William J. Hughes Technical Center. The Contractor shall comply with formal administrative requirements and security compliance obligations prior to entering the TSL Campus. The project is located within the NJ Pinelands reserve. title: Lease for office space - 6,533 sq ft required
description: SOLICITATION FOR OFFER LOCATION: Menomonee Falls/Milwaukee/Butler/Lannon, Wisconsin Delineated Area N Boundary: _County Line Road______ S Boundary: _Silver Spring Drive______ E Boundary: _North 107th Street_______ W Boundary: _Lannon Road__________ The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Recruiting Facilities Program, is soliciting offers for 6,533 square feet (useable) of office space within the delineated area. Space will need to be capable of accommodating the floor plan requirements as shown on the attached template (including secondary egress); have adequate parking (prefer it is sign designated) for 9 Governments-owned vehicles 24 hours a day/7 days a week, as well as adequate parking within 4 blocks for employees and customer vehicles; include daytime janitorial services; include adequate signage for maximum visibility; and lessor needs to secure three bids for the build-out of the space to meet the construction specifications provided. Sites that are located adjacent to adult entertainment shops (i.e. bookstores, video stores, or theatres), night clubs/bars, methadone clinics, drug rehabilitation centers, marijuana/hemp dispensaries, medical marijuana dispensaries, gun shops, liquor stores, etc. could potentially be eliminated from competition as these are considered non-compatible businesses. Lessors are required to be registered and active in www.sam.gov prior to the deadline for final officer submission. Offers will need to include a completed RPW (Rental Proposal Worksheet), proof of registration in www.sam.gov (i.e. active CAGE code), a proposed floor plan and the construction bids for build-out meeting the construction specifications. Attached is a copy of the lease document. The general clauses, the construction specifications, the janitorial specifications, the RPW, instructions for SAM (System for Award Management) registration, and a floor plan template. Please thoroughly review all documents and make sure that you agree to the terms presented. The government lease and the general clauses are standard are for the most part, not negotiable, and must be accepted as written and shown on the attached file. Review the constructions specifications completely as they stipulate additional lessor responsibilities. Three construction bids for the build-out are requested. After a bid is accepted, no change orders are authorized, so bids need to be accurate and complete (including taxes and fees). Special attention should be given to security requirements (video entry control system, closed circuit television system and video recording, dual roller shades on exterior windows, fixed panel shades on exterior entry door and peep hole in secondary exit, perforated window wrap), fragmentation film on exterior window/glass doors, telecommunication wiring requirements, addition of water fountain, signage, paint, wall graphics, phone jacks, electrical outlets and special carpet tiles. These are items that can add significant cost and may be overlooked in the bid process; however, all items in the specifications need to be followed, even if the code does not require the item (i.e. smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, etc.). Bids shall include any tear down/haul away expenses. The attached floor plan is to be used as a generalized idea and reference tool for close proximity of amount of useable space, this location will require for build out in ALL space. Submitted floor plans must meet the space requirements as designated on attached examples. It is mandatory that janitorial services be included in the lease (lessor responsible for contracting these services). Be sure to review the attached janitorial guidance and ensure the costs of these services are included on the rental proposal worksheet. Leases are negotiated for a 5 year term, but they include a clause stating the Government can terminate giving reasonable days� notice. In order to incorporate firm term years, meaning the Government cannot get out of the lease for a specified period of time, we ask the lessor to provide a significant contribution towards the build out costs. Five year firm term leases are generally not considered. Following are the factors that will be considered when evaluating bids/offers: Location Ability to meet all construction specifications, security measures and lease requirements Complete initial and final offers must be received by a defined deadline Competitive costs in the best interest of the government Qualitative ratings by client submission Sites should not be located adjacent to adult entertainment shops (i.e. bookstores, video stores, or theatres), night clubs/bars, methadone clinics, drug rehabilitation centers, marijuana/hemp dispensaries, medical marijuana dispensaries, gun shops, liquor stores, etc., and could potentially be eliminated from competition as these are considered non-compatible businesses Initial offers are due no later than close of business on October 16, 2026 (30 calendar days from the advertisement in SAM.GOV). You will receive feedback of your initial offer identifying missing items/weaknesses by October 21, 2026 (5 calendar days after initial closing date). After receiving feedback, your best and final offer will be due no later than close of business on October 31, 2026 (10 calendar days after feedback provided). If you have a location that meets the required criteria and interested in consideration, please email the provided USACE member in this advertisement with: Location Address Sq. Ft. Available Point of contact information of your representative Once confirmed this location meets the minimum requirements, you will be contacted to set up an appointment for a site visit. All locations that meet the criteria will be given the opportunity to solicit a bid for award, provided no other circumstances during the site visit uncover a reason (deemed disqualified by USACE personnel) to eliminate the site from contention.

description: DESCRIPTION 1. Solicitation Statement This is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). A pre-solicitation synopsis is not required for this acquisition in accordance with RFO Part 5.101.1(b)(1)(i). This requirement is being solicited utilizing the streamlined commercial acquisition procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1(c)(2) (Simplified procedures) to promote competition to the maximum extent practicable. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. 2. Description of Requirement The 325th Contracting Squadron at Tyndall AFB, FL, requires a contractor to furnish all labor, materials, transportation, and equipment necessary to service and relocate government-owned portable latrines and handwash stations at Tyndall AFB, FL. Services support Tyndall AFB rebuild efforts, Silver Flag student field training, 53 WEG full-scale drone launches, and Force Support Squadron (FSS) recreational areas. The contract will consist of a one-year base period with three (3) one-year option periods (Anticipated Period of Performance: 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030). 3. Schedule of Items (CLINs) Offerors must submit pricing for all of the following Contract Line Items (CLINs) using Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: CLIN 0001 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Base Support Area. Quantity: 16 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0002 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Silver Flag Area. Quantity: 15 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0003 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Handwash Stations; Base-Wide. Quantity: 5 units. Weekly restocking and cleaning. CLIN 0004 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; 53 WEG Area. Quantity: 4 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0005 (Base Year): Relocation of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 relocation actions per year). CLIN 0006 (Base Year): Additional Servicing of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 additional servicing actions per year). CLINs 1001�3006: Repeat the above CLIN structure for Option Years 1, 2, and 3. 4. Instructions to Offerors (Addendum to 52.212-1) To be considered for award, offerors must submit their quotes in two (2) separate volumes via email to fidencio.posadas@us.af.mil and cleville.yarbrough@us.af.mil no later than the Close Date of 01 October 2026 at 3:30 PM CST. Late or incomplete quotes will not be evaluated. Volume 1 � Price Quote: Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: Complete all unit prices for CLINs X001 through X006 across the Base Period and Option Years 1, 2, and 3. The worksheet will automatically compute the Total Evaluated Price (TEP). Solicitation Acknowledgement: Complete offeror identification details (CAGE code, Unique Entity ID [UEI], business size/socioeconomic status) and acknowledge all amendments, if issued. Provisions Fill-ins: Return any solicitation provisions requiring vendor fill-ins. title: Tyndall Portable Latrine Servicing - 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030
description: DESCRIPTION 1. Solicitation Statement This is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). A pre-solicitation synopsis is not required for this acquisition in accordance with RFO Part 5.101.1(b)(1)(i). This requirement is being solicited utilizing the streamlined commercial acquisition procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1(c)(2) (Simplified procedures) to promote competition to the maximum extent practicable. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. 2. Description of Requirement The 325th Contracting Squadron at Tyndall AFB, FL, requires a contractor to furnish all labor, materials, transportation, and equipment necessary to service and relocate government-owned portable latrines and handwash stations at Tyndall AFB, FL. Services support Tyndall AFB rebuild efforts, Silver Flag student field training, 53 WEG full-scale drone launches, and Force Support Squadron (FSS) recreational areas. The contract will consist of a one-year base period with three (3) one-year option periods (Anticipated Period of Performance: 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030). 3. Schedule of Items (CLINs) Offerors must submit pricing for all of the following Contract Line Items (CLINs) using Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: CLIN 0001 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Base Support Area. Quantity: 16 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0002 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Silver Flag Area. Quantity: 15 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0003 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Handwash Stations; Base-Wide. Quantity: 5 units. Weekly restocking and cleaning. CLIN 0004 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; 53 WEG Area. Quantity: 4 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0005 (Base Year): Relocation of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 relocation actions per year). CLIN 0006 (Base Year): Additional Servicing of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 additional servicing actions per year). CLINs 1001�3006: Repeat the above CLIN structure for Option Years 1, 2, and 3. 4. Instructions to Offerors (Addendum to 52.212-1) To be considered for award, offerors must submit their quotes in two (2) separate volumes via email to fidencio.posadas@us.af.mil and cleville.yarbrough@us.af.mil no later than the Close Date of 01 October 2026 at 3:30 PM CST. Late or incomplete quotes will not be evaluated. Volume 1 � Price Quote: Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: Complete all unit prices for CLINs X001 through X006 across the Base Period and Option Years 1, 2, and 3. The worksheet will automatically compute the Total Evaluated Price (TEP). Solicitation Acknowledgement: Complete offeror identification details (CAGE code, Unique Entity ID [UEI], business size/socioeconomic status) and acknowledge all amendments, if issued. Provisions Fill-ins: Return any solicitation provisions requiring vendor fill-ins. Note on Extension: In accordance with the evaluation terms, the Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will not include a separate priced line item for the 6-month extension period authorized by FAR 52.217-8; any extension executed under this clause will be based on the prevailing rates of the most recent option period. Volume 2 � Technical Capability Proposal: Technical Approach and Equipment: A clear narrative detailing the offerors approach, equipment (e.g., pump trucks, service vehicles), materials, and staffing plan necessary to perform all pumping, sanitizing, restocking, and relocation tasks in compliance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS).(Max 5 Pages) Safety Data Sheets (SDS / MSDS): Provide copies of Safety Data Sheets for all cleaning, sanitizing, and deodorizing chemicals proposed for use. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email to the points of contact listed above no later than 21 September 2026 at 1:00 PM CST. Questions received after this cutoff may not be answered. 5. Evaluation for Award (Addendum to 52.212-2) In accordance with RFO Part 12.203 (Evaluation) and simplified commercial procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1, the Government will award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order/contract to the responsible small business offeror whose conforming quote represents the Best Value to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following evaluation factors will be utilized: Factor 1: Technical Acceptability (Pass/Fail): A quote will be rated technically acceptable if the proposal demonstrates: Sufficient equipment, vehicles, labor, and capability to perform all weekly servicing and ad-hoc relocations in accordance with the PWS. A thorough understanding of the requirement and operational constraints at Tyndall AFB. Submission of acceptable Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all sanitation and deodorizing chemicals. Factor 2: Price: Quotes will be reviewed for price reasonableness through competition. The Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will be the sum of all CLINs (CLINs X001�X006) for the Base Year and Option Years 1 through 3, calculated on Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet. Award Basis: The Government intends to evaluate quotes and make an award without discussions. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct communications or clarifications if determined to be in its best interest. 6. Attachments Attachment 1 - PWS 19 August 2026 - Latrine Servicing Attachment 2 - WD 2015-4559 Rev 34 Attachment 3 - Portable Latrine Map Attachment 4 - Pricing Worksheet FA481926Q0093

title: Tyndall Portable Latrine Servicing - 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030
description: DESCRIPTION 1. Solicitation Statement This is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). A pre-solicitation synopsis is not required for this acquisition in accordance with RFO Part 5.101.1(b)(1)(i). This requirement is being solicited utilizing the streamlined commercial acquisition procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1(c)(2) (Simplified procedures) to promote competition to the maximum extent practicable. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. 2. Description of Requirement The 325th Contracting Squadron at Tyndall AFB, FL, requires a contractor to furnish all labor, materials, transportation, and equipment necessary to service and relocate government-owned portable latrines and handwash stations at Tyndall AFB, FL. Services support Tyndall AFB rebuild efforts, Silver Flag student field training, 53 WEG full-scale drone launches, and Force Support Squadron (FSS) recreational areas. The contract will consist of a one-year base period with three (3) one-year option periods (Anticipated Period of Performance: 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030). 3. Schedule of Items (CLINs) Offerors must submit pricing for all of the following Contract Line Items (CLINs) using Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: CLIN 0001 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Base Support Area. Quantity: 16 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0002 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Silver Flag Area. Quantity: 15 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0003 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Handwash Stations; Base-Wide. Quantity: 5 units. Weekly restocking and cleaning. CLIN 0004 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; 53 WEG Area. Quantity: 4 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0005 (Base Year): Relocation of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 relocation actions per year). CLIN 0006 (Base Year): Additional Servicing of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 additional servicing actions per year). CLINs 1001�3006: Repeat the above CLIN structure for Option Years 1, 2, and 3. 4. Instructions to Offerors (Addendum to 52.212-1) To be considered for award, offerors must submit their quotes in two (2) separate volumes via email to fidencio.posadas@us.af.mil and cleville.yarbrough@us.af.mil no later than the Close Date of 01 October 2026 at 3:30 PM CST. Late or incomplete quotes will not be evaluated. Volume 1 � Price Quote: Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: Complete all unit prices for CLINs X001 through X006 across the Base Period and Option Years 1, 2, and 3. The worksheet will automatically compute the Total Evaluated Price (TEP). Solicitation Acknowledgement: Complete offeror identification details (CAGE code, Unique Entity ID [UEI], business size/socioeconomic status) and acknowledge all amendments, if issued. Provisions Fill-ins: Return any solicitation provisions requiring vendor fill-ins. Note on Extension: In accordance with the evaluation terms, the Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will not include a separate priced line item for the 6-month extension period authorized by FAR 52.217-8; any extension executed under this clause will be based on the prevailing rates of the most recent option period. Volume 2 � Technical Capability Proposal: Technical Approach and Equipment: A clear narrative detailing the offerors approach, equipment (e.g., pump trucks, service vehicles), materials, and staffing plan necessary to perform all pumping, sanitizing, restocking, and relocation tasks in compliance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS).(Max 5 Pages) Safety Data Sheets (SDS / MSDS): Provide copies of Safety Data Sheets for all cleaning, sanitizing, and deodorizing chemicals proposed for use. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email to the points of contact listed above no later than 21 September 2026 at 1:00 PM CST. Questions received after this cutoff may not be answered. 5. Evaluation for Award (Addendum to 52.212-2) In accordance with RFO Part 12.203 (Evaluation) and simplified commercial procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1, the Government will award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order/contract to the responsible small business offeror whose conforming quote represents the Best Value to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following evaluation factors will be utilized: Factor 1: Technical Acceptability (Pass/Fail): A quote will be rated technically acceptable if the proposal demonstrates: Sufficient equipment, vehicles, labor, and capability to perform all weekly servicing and ad-hoc relocations in accordance with the PWS. A thorough understanding of the requirement and operational constraints at Tyndall AFB. Submission of acceptable Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all sanitation and deodorizing chemicals. Factor 2: Price: Quotes will be reviewed for price reasonableness through competition. The Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will be the sum of all CLINs (CLINs X001�X006) for the Base Year and Option Years 1 through 3, calculated on Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet. Award Basis: The Government intends to evaluate quotes and make an award without discussions. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct communications or clarifications if determined to be in its best interest. 6. Attachments Attachment 1 - PWS 19 August 2026 - Latrine Servicing Attachment 2 - WD 2015-4559 Rev 34 Attachment 3 - Portable Latrine Map Attachment 4 - Pricing Worksheet FA481926Q0093

description: DESCRIPTION 1. Solicitation Statement This is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). A pre-solicitation synopsis is not required for this acquisition in accordance with RFO Part 5.101.1(b)(1)(i). This requirement is being solicited utilizing the streamlined commercial acquisition procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1(c)(2) (Simplified procedures) to promote competition to the maximum extent practicable. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. 2. Description of Requirement The 325th Contracting Squadron at Tyndall AFB, FL, requires a contractor to furnish all labor, materials, transportation, and equipment necessary to service and relocate government-owned portable latrines and handwash stations at Tyndall AFB, FL. Services support Tyndall AFB rebuild efforts, Silver Flag student field training, 53 WEG full-scale drone launches, and Force Support Squadron (FSS) recreational areas. The contract will consist of a one-year base period with three (3) one-year option periods (Anticipated Period of Performance: 6 December 2026 to 5 December 2030). 3. Schedule of Items (CLINs) Offerors must submit pricing for all of the following Contract Line Items (CLINs) using Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: CLIN 0001 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Base Support Area. Quantity: 16 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0002 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; Silver Flag Area. Quantity: 15 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0003 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Handwash Stations; Base-Wide. Quantity: 5 units. Weekly restocking and cleaning. CLIN 0004 (Base Year): Service of Government-Owned Portable Latrines; 53 WEG Area. Quantity: 4 units. Weekly waste removal and cleaning. CLIN 0005 (Base Year): Relocation of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 relocation actions per year). CLIN 0006 (Base Year): Additional Servicing of Government-Owned Portable Latrines and Handwash Stations (Estimated 50 additional servicing actions per year). CLINs 1001�3006: Repeat the above CLIN structure for Option Years 1, 2, and 3. 4. Instructions to Offerors (Addendum to 52.212-1) To be considered for award, offerors must submit their quotes in two (2) separate volumes via email to fidencio.posadas@us.af.mil and cleville.yarbrough@us.af.mil no later than the Close Date of 01 October 2026 at 3:30 PM CDT (Local Tyndall AFB Time). Late or incomplete quotes will not be evaluated. Volume 1 � Price Quote: Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet: Complete all unit prices for CLINs X001 through X006 across the Base Period and Option Years 1, 2, and 3. The worksheet will automatically compute the Total Evaluated Price (TEP). Solicitation Acknowledgement: Complete offeror identification details (CAGE code, Unique Entity ID [UEI], business size/socioeconomic status) and acknowledge all amendments, if issued. Provisions Fill-ins: Return any solicitation provisions requiring vendor fill-ins. Note on Extension: In accordance with the evaluation terms, the Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will not include a separate priced line item for the 6-month extension period authorized by FAR 52.217-8; any extension executed under this clause will be based on the prevailing rates of the most recent option period. Volume 2 � Technical Capability Proposal: Technical Approach and Equipment: A clear narrative detailing the offerors approach, equipment (e.g., pump trucks, service vehicles), materials, and staffing plan necessary to perform all pumping, sanitizing, restocking, and relocation tasks in compliance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS).(Max 5 Pages) Safety Data Sheets (SDS / MSDS): Provide copies of Safety Data Sheets for all cleaning, sanitizing, and deodorizing chemicals proposed for use. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email to the points of contact listed above no later than 21 September 2026 at 1:00 PM CDT (Local Tyndall AFB Time). Questions received after this cutoff may not be answered. 5. Evaluation for Award (Addendum to 52.212-2) In accordance with RFO Part 12.203 (Evaluation) and simplified commercial procedures under RFO Part 12.201-1, the Government will award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order/contract to the responsible small business offeror whose conforming quote represents the Best Value to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following evaluation factors will be utilized: Factor 1: Technical Acceptability (Pass/Fail): A quote will be rated technically acceptable if the proposal demonstrates: Sufficient equipment, vehicles, labor, and capability to perform all weekly servicing and ad-hoc relocations in accordance with the PWS. A thorough understanding of the requirement and operational constraints at Tyndall AFB. Submission of acceptable Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all sanitation and deodorizing chemicals. Factor 2: Price: Quotes will be reviewed for price reasonableness through competition. The Total Evaluated Price (TEP) will be the sum of all CLINs (CLINs X001�X006) for the Base Year and Option Years 1 through 3, calculated on Attachment 4 � Pricing Worksheet. Award Basis: The Government intends to evaluate quotes and make an award without discussions. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct communications or clarifications if determined to be in its best interest. 6. title: Ryhmäkasvien ja kevätkukkien hankinta Turun ja Kaarinan seurakuntayhtymän hautausmaille
description: Ryhmäkasvien ja kevätkukkien hankinta Turun ja Kaarinan seurakuntayhtymän hautausmaille Hankittavina tuotteina ovat ryhmäkasvien, äitienpäiväruusujen ja kevätkrysanteemien taimet toimitettuna Turun ja Kaarinan seurakuntayhtymän hautausmaille vuodelle 2027 ja optiona vuodelle 2028. Sopimus jatkuu automaattisesti vuodelle 2028 (optiovuosi) ellei jompikumpi osapuoli irtisano sopimusta 30.8.2027 mennessä. Hankittavien taimien määrä noin 49 000 kpl / vuosi. Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhtä tai useampaa kokonaista tuoteriviä. Tuoterivejä on kaikkiaan 14 kpl. Kasvilajit, - lajikkeet, värit ja ruukkukoot on lueteltu tarjouslomakkeessa (Liite 3). Äitienpäiväruusut, kevätkrysanteemit ja pääosa ryhmäkasveista toimitetaan Turun hautausmaalle osoitteeseen: Turun ja Kaarinan seurakuntayhtymän huoltokeskus Skarppakullantie 10 20720 Turku. Pienempiä taimimääriä (koskee ryhmäkasvien toimituksia) toimitetaan lisäksi seuraaville hautausmaille: Katariinan hautausmaa Kirkkotie 46 20540 Turku Kärsämäen hautausmaa Vahdontie 3 20360 Turku Piikkiön hautausmaa Hadvalantie 5 21500 Piikkiö Toimitusmäärä Katariinaan on noin 3700 kpl, Kärsämäkeen noin 2300 kpl ja Piikkiöön noin 1000 kpl. Taimitoimitukset tulee tehdä arkipäivisin kello 7–15. Toimituksissa on huomioitava, että eri lajikkeita ja värejä tulee toimittaa joka toimituspäivä määrällisesti samassa suhteessa, kuin mikä on niiden osuus tilauksen kokonaismäärästä. Näin siksi, että tilaaja aloittaa taimien istutuksen heti toimituspäivästä alkaen. Toimitukset vuodelle 2027 ajoittuvat seuraavasti (vuoden 2028 päivämäärät sovitaan erikseen): Äitienpäiväruusujen ja kevätkrysanteemien toimituspäivä on maanantai 3.5.2027 tai sopimuksen mukaan. Ryhmäkasvitoimitukset aloitetaan Turun hautausmaalle maanantaina 31.5.2027. Ensimmäiset erät voi tuoda Turun hautausmaalle sovitusti jo sunnuntaina 30.5.2027. Toimituksesta tulee sopia 7 päivää ennen. Kesäkuun koko toimitusmäärästä (koskee kaikkia lajeja, lajikkeita ja värejä) vähintään puolet on toimitettava perille tiistaihin 1.6 klo 15 mennessä. Pienemmille hautausmaille toimitukset tulee toteuttaa kerralla tiistaina 1.6. Tilaaja tarkentaa toimitusten määrät eri toimitusosoitteisiin viimeistään toimitusten alkamista edeltävällä viikolla. Kesäkuun kokonaistoimitusmäärästä 75 % tulee olla toimitettu torstaihin 3.6 kello 15 mennessä ja koko tilauksen tulee olla toimitettu viimeistään tiistaina 8.6 kello 15. Ns. paikkaustaimien toimitukset tehdään 6.7.2027 tai sopimuksen mukaan. Vuoden 2028 osalta toimitusajat ovat pääpiirteissään samat kuin vuonna 2027. Taimet toimitetaan rullakoissa kuljetusalustoihin pakattuna. Rullakot voi noutaa takaisin viimeistään 2 viikon kuluttua toimituksesta.,

description: In line with the Army�s Modernization Strategy, the Army must modernize sustainment practices and capabilities as it delivers the Army of 2030 / develops the Army of 2040. The Army is committed to targeted modernization to assure power projection, maximize geographic flexibility, reduce response times to aid allies and partners, and protect national objectives. For forces in the fight, sustainment determines the depth, breadth, and duration of operations. Therefore, modernization of the sustainment warfighting function is required to ensure freedom of action, extend operational reach, and prolong endurance of Soldiers and units in the field. To maintain excellence and consistently improve sustainment of deployed forces, the Army seeks to leverage several advancements. Acquisition of commercial sustainment and manufacturing technologies and services will accelerate Army Aviation and Missile Command�s (AMCOM) capabilities to get advanced solutions to the Warfighter while enhancing and optimizing the Headquarters, Field, and Defense Manufacturing Base�s capabilities for today and tomorrow�s missions. With the focus on both �new capabilities� and �operational constructs� convergent manufacturing technologies will accelerate the OIB�s capability to get advanced solutions to the Warfighter while enhancing and optimizing the Defense Manufacturing Base for today and tomorrow�s missions. Manufacturing excellence is critical for Army technology dominance and force projection to increase the �Speed of Battle.� This CSO will utilize a solicitation process authorized by 10 U.S.C. � 3458 and implemented by RFO DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under this CSO, the DoW will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial products and services. title: Market Survey for OFB-2072-A1 Image Intensifier Assembly
description: Sources sought to provide the government with the OFB-2072-A1 Image Intensifier Assembly (NSN: 5855-01-712-2987), for the U.S. Military. The AN/PSQ-42 & AN/PSQ-43 are helmet-mounted, battery-operated systems that combine the light amplification capability of night vision devices with the heat sensing capability of thermal imaging devices. They allow for observation and target identification under adverse conditions including light rain, light smoke, light snow, and low light to total darkness. The AN/PSQ-42 & AN/PSQ-43 combines the light amplification capability of image intensification devices with the heat sensing capability of thermal imaging systems. Requirements Description: The United States Army is looking for sources with the ability to provide the OFB-2072-A1 Image Intensifier Tube, (NSN: 5855-01-712-2987) for the AN/PSQ-42 & AN/PSQ-43. The Government requires an estimated quantity of 2,300 OFB-2072-A1 Image Intensifier Tubes (NSN: 5855-01-712-2987) over a 5-year period. This is not a solicitation. This is only an estimate and will not bind the contractor or the Government in any way or at any time into a contract with any of the specified terms below. Suppliers capable of supplying these items, in accordance with the government data package and in the quantities specified above, should contact the government before September 24, 2026. Submissions can be sent to michelet.audige.civ@army.mil. Responses must include a list of items the supplier is able to produce or source as well as documentation that the supplier can provide the army with a physically and functionally component from the list above. Examples of such documentation can be test results, copy of purchase orders if the supplier was a vendor to the listed source, or a statement from listed source demonstrating that the supplier can provide the Army a solution. For more information contact Michelet Audige at michelet.audige.civ@army.mil. Items and/or Services to Be Procured: NSN: 5855-01-712-2987 NOMENCLATURE: Image Intensifier Tube PART NUMBER: OFB-2072-A1 CAGE: OB107 Requested Response Information: We request that sources who can manufacture the listed parts or services submit information to show their capability. At a minimum the support information you submit should include, but is not limited to, the following types of documentation: Questionnaire, information on previous Government and commercial contracts, and evidence that the item can be provided. In your response, please include your company name, CAGE code, and a technical point of contact with email address and telephone number. title: Advanced GNSS Simulator
description: *****This announcement is not a formal Request for Quotes (RFQ). This SSN/RFI is for informational and planning purposes only and does not guarantee that an award will be made. Any quotes submitted in response to this SSN/RFI are not quotes on which an order will be issued. The Government assumes NO financial responsibility for any costs incurred. A solicitation package is not available at this time. However, should such a requirement materialize, no basis for claims against NRL shall arise as a result of a response to this SSN/RFI or NRL�s use of such information either as part of our evaluation process or in developing specifications or work statements for any subsequent requirement. PURPOSE AND ACQUISITION BACKGROUND The purpose of this notice is to identify potential industry sources capable of delivering a high-precision, multi-channel Advanced Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Simulator suite. This requirement will support critical Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) research, development, and testing spanning dual-frequency GPS baselines, encrypted military signals (SAASM and AES M-Code), full-spectrum multi-constellations, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Alternative Navigation (ALTNAV), lunar S-band PNT, contested/threat environments, and multi-element Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) wavefront testing. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS & TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS The required capability consists of a minimum of two (2) discrete simulation units meeting the essential physical, electrical, and functional characteristics detailed below. Essential Physical and Electrical Characteristics (Applicable to Both Units) Essential Physical Characteristics Mounts in standard width 19-inch rack mount and includes mounting brackets. Mountable rack units less than or equal to 27 inches of depth. Stable operation over temperature range of 10degC to 40degC and 40% to 90% relative humidity, non-condensing. RF output ports are located on front and rear of chassis and are Type N female connector. RF connector ports are all 50-ohm impedance. Minimum of one combined RF output Type N female connector for high-power generation (+50dB above nominal). BNC female connector for 1 Pulse Per Second (PPS) input for syncing to external pulse. BNC female connector for 1 Pulse Per Second (PPS) output from simulator to provides a precise hardware timing reference signal of the simulated UTC second. BNC female connector for trigger input port to start or synchronize a scenario run. BNC female connector for an external 10 MHz reference input. BNC female connector for 10Mhz internal reference output. At least four (4) Universal Serial Bus (USB Type-A, 3.0 or higher) ports on rear panel and 2 USB (Type-A, 3.0 or higher) ports on front panel for I/O connections. At least one video interface option must be DisplayPort (DP 1.4a or higher) or High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI 2.1 or higher). Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 or higher included on computer to address Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) requirements. Essential Functional Characteristics (Operational, Behavioral, Software Capabilities) At a minimum, two separate units are needed. The first unit must simulate the constellations listed below and simulate a receiver in a stationary (static) position or in a moving (dynamic) position either on the earth or in a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) around the earth. Global Positioning System (GPS) � including the Selective Availability Anti-spoofing Module (SAASM) classified package and M-code L1 � 1575.42MHz L2 � 1227.6MHz L5 � 1176.45MHz Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS) L1 � 1598.06MHz to 1609.31MHz L2 � 1242.9375MHz to 1251.6875 MHz BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) B1I � 1561.098MHz B2I � 1207.14MHz Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System E1 � 1575.42MHz E5a � 1176.45MHz E5b � 1207.14MHz E6 � 1278.52MHz Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) L5 � 1176.45MHz S-band � 2492.028MHz QZSS L1 � 1575.42MHz L2 � 1227.6MHz L5 � 1176.45MHz Alternative Navigation (ALTNAV) Simulate Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite signals used for commercial and military alternative navigation. Emulates non-GNSS radio frequency sources, including ground-based transmitters. Lunar PNT 2483.5 � 2500 MHz S-band range, XONA Space system emulation X1 � 1591.2MHz � 1595MHz X5 � 1180.4MHz � 1200.6MHz � Integrated commercial low Earth orbit (LEO) production signals bundle software (designed specifically to generate and test next-generation LEO-based PNT waveforms such as Xona). System 2 (Multi-Output & Secure PNT for CRPA Testing) The second unit must simulate only the GPS constellation below and still simulate a receiver in a stationary position(static) or in a moving(dynamic) position either on the earth or in a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) around the earth. Global Positioning System (GPS) � including the Selective Availability Anti-spoofing Module (SAASM) classified package and M-code L1 � 1575.42MHz L2 � 1227.6MHz L5 � 1176.45MHz � Minimum of 4 element Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) testing capability. The platform is required to emulate the synchronous, phase coherent and spatially correct RF wavefront as received at each element of a CRPA. REQUIRED CONTRACTOR RESPONSE FORMAT: Interested parties, at a minimum, shall supply all of the below required information in a Capability Statement. 1. CONTACT INFORMATION: a) Company Name and Address b) Point of Contact for questions/clarification c) Telephone Number and e-mail address d) CAGE Code, and business size e) NAICS and PSC Code of the proposed solution (SEE https://psctool.us) f) Business Size Standard /Socioeconomic Categories 2. TECHNICAL INFORMATION: a) List of capabilities/resources relevant to the above specifications. b) Questions for the Technical team regarding changes/suggestions to the specification list to add clarity. (Questions will not receive a response but will be provided to the technical team for consideration in preparing the final specification.) 3. COMMERCIALITY OF PROPOSED ITEM: a) Whether item(s) offered/proposed is a commercial item offered by your company and/or customarily used by the general public or non-government entities for other than Government purposes. b) Whether the item has been sold, leased, or licensed to the general public, and if so, identify one or more such sales, leases, or licenses to document the commerciality of the item. 4. PRODUCT DESCRIPTION: a) Provide a description of how the proposed product will meet or exceed each of the required technical specifications. b) Provide a product brochure and highlight the areas that meet or exceed specifications. 5. PAST PERFORMANCE: A list of contracts or task orders that are similar to that required under the attached Specification. 6. MULTIPLE AWARD SCHEUDLE CONTRACT: a) Indicate whether products and services are all available on a GSA contract, or similar vehicle. b) Provide applicable GSA or other contract number. 7. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT DETAILS: Responses should be no more than 5-7 pages.

title: DLA Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) FY2026
description: A. Summary of Amendment 004 1. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is conducting a commercial solutions opening (CSO) authorized by 10 U.S.C. � 3458 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement, Subpart 212.70, Defense Commercial Solutions Opening. DLA intends to solicit Solution Briefs in response to the addendum Areas of Interest (AOIs), which DLA may change, amend, open, and close from time to time at DLA�s sole discretion. Interested offerors are encouraged to frequently check this CSO from new or revised AOIs. DLA intends to keep this CSO SP4701-24-S-C001 open until 01 October 2026 ; however, DLA reserves the right to close this CSO at any time. 2. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 3458(c)(2), any contract or agreement DLA may award under pursuant to this CSO shall be fixed-price. DLA intends to award commercial contracts in accordance with DFARS 212.7002(b); however, DLA may, at DLA�s discretion, to award an other transaction agreement in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. 3. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact: Mr. Thomas Walsh Agreements and Contracting Officer DLA DCSO-P5 Thomas.Walsh@dla.mil Mrs. Lauren Runowski Agreements and Contracting Specialist DLA DCSO-P5 lauren.runowski@dla.mil 4. DLA provides no funding for any offer submitted to this CSO. DLA funding is only possible after a signed contract. B. Background: DLA is the Department of Defense�s logistics combat support activity. DLA provides worldwide logistical support to the military services and other authorized customers, which may include civilian organizations and foreign countries. Potential offerors may learn more about DLA at htts://www.dla.mil. C. How to Submit a Solution Brief. Prior to the closing date of the published Area of Interest, electronically submit to the person identified in paragraph A.3. of this CSO an unclassified Solution Brief, utilizing the Solution Brief template at Attachment 1. Mark as appropriate all parts of the Solution Brief considered proprietary. By submitting a Solution Brief, the offeror agrees to DFARS 252.227-7016, Rights in Bid or Proposal Information. The Solution Brief must �stand alone�. While the Solution Brief may include references to outside materials, links to website, etc., DLA WILL NOT AND CAN NOT consider such material. Similarly, DLA will not consider any accompanying slides, sales materials, integrated or outside videos, or the like sent with the Solution Brief. DLA may reject, without further consideration, Solution Briefs sent with extraneous materials. Offerors may submit multiple Solution Briefs for each AOI. While each Solution Brief may reference another Solution Brief, DLA WILL NOT AND CAN NOT consider that referenced Solution Brief in evaluating this submitted Solution Brief. Solution Briefs� prices and all other terms and conditions must remain valid for 180 calendar days from the submission date of the Solution Brief. D. How DLA Will Make Any Awards. 1. DLA will first review Solution Briefs for conformance with this CSO. DLA will return Solution Briefs DLA finds not in conformance with this CSO. The offeror may, if the date and time stated in the Area of Interest has not passed, re-submit a revised Solution Brief. While DLA intends to complete this review diligently, DLA is under no obligation to complete this review soon enough for an offeror to submit a revised Solution Brief. Therefore, offerors should submit their best, conforming, Solution Briefs. 2. For Solution Briefs both received before the closing time of CSO and AOI, and also conforming to the CSO, DLA subject-matter expert technical evaluators will evaluate the Solution Brief. First, evaluators will evaluate Factor 1, Possibility of Funding, and rate the Solution Brief as either �Funding Possible� or �Funding Not Possible�. If evaluated as �Funding Not Possible,� evaluators will not evaluate the Solution Brief further and DLA will notify the offeror. If evaluated as �Funding Possible,� evaluators will continue their evaluations through the remaining factors, assigning each remaining factor one of the following ratings: �Exceptional,� �Good,� �Acceptable,� �Marginal,� or �Unacceptable.� All evaluation factors are described below. a. Factor 1: Possibility of Funding. Does funding reasonably exist to fund the proposed solution? Solutions with lower prices are favored. b. Factor 2: Technical Feasibility. How technically feasible is the proposed solution to an AOI, given the present state of the technology and science? Solutions with a lower technological risk profile are favored. c. Factor 3: Responsiveness. How responsive is the proposed solution to the AOI? Solutions responsive to the problem identified in the AOI, without creating new problems, are favored. d. Factor 4: Viability. How viable is the proposed solution given existing organizational and regulatory environments? Solutions compatible with existing DLA, DoD, and federal policies, processes, and procedures, are favored. e. Factor 5: Desirability. How desirable is the proposed solution to the eventual end-user? Solutions easily adaptable, useful, and implementable are favored. 3. After the above evaluation, the technical evaluators will then decide whether the solution proposed in the Solution Brief merits further consideration. Note that while Solution Briefs are not evaluated against other Solution Briefs, DLA has limited funding and acquisition manpower and thus cannot pursue all otherwise meritorious Solution Briefs. DLA also recognizes that industry resources in pursing business with DLA are limited. To the extent DLA must select between highly rated Solution Briefs to pursue further, DLA will aggregate the Factor 2 through 5 ratings together equally to discern the most highly rated Solution Briefs. If further discernment is necessary amongst highly rated Solution Briefs, DLA will then additionally consider the Factor 2 through 5 ratings in order of importance, with Factor 2 being the most important, Factor 3 being the second most important, Factor 4 being the third most important, and Factor 5 being the fourth most important. And if still additional discernment is necessary, DLA will then consider the price proposed in the Solution Brief and select for further consideration the lowest priced Solution Brief. 4. If the technical evaluators decide a proposed Solution Brief merits further consideration, technical evaluators will decide whether to further consider the proposed solution via a Pitch, Full Proposal, or both. Technical evaluators may also decide a Pitch or Full Proposal, or both, are unnecessary, and refer a Solution Brief for negotiation of a possible award as described in paragraph 5. a. Pitch: DLA would invite the offeror to �pitch� the offeror�s proposed solution in a presentation, whether via a remote meeting, a face-to-face meeting, or other mutually agreeable means. DLA will advise the offeror of the parameters of the Pitch at that time. Offerors may propose different parameters; however, the final decision rests with DLA, as represented by the person noted in paragraph A(3). During the Pitch, the parties may verbally discuss the proposed solution. After the Pitch, DLA will decide whether an additional Pitch is desired, to request a full proposal, refer the offeror to the supporting contracting activity for award negotiations, or to terminate further consideration of the offer. b. Full Proposal: DLA would invite the offeror to submit a full proposal. DLA will advise the offeror of the parameters of the full proposal at that time. Offerors may propose different parameters; however, the final decision rests with DLA. After receipt of the Full Proposal, DLA may communicate with the offeror about the Full Proposal, to better understand and review it. After reviewing the Full Proposal, DLA will decide whether an additional or revised Full Proposal is desired, to request a �Pitch�, refer the offeror to the supporting contracting activity for award negotiations, or

The requirement aims to provide support to AAQ with government acquisition document preparation and other administrative support services to facilitate the completion of the growing acquisition workload across the FAA. This contract does not permit contractor employees to perform inherently governmental duties, such as obligating appropriated funds or executing contractual agreements or modifications on behalf of the agency. Individual AAQ organizations are expected to place their own orders under this contract at various times throughout the ordering period. It is currently anticipated that the contract types to be used will consist primarily of Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for all full-time equivalent contractor support personnel, along with a small capability (no more than 5% of the total contract value) for Labor Hours (LH) to support minor transitional or surge needs; however, this is still subject to change. All information in this announcement is tentative and subject to change if and when a solicitation is released. The FAA currently anticipates releasing a solicitation sometime in late summer to mid-fall of 2026. INDUSTRY FEEDBACK REQUESTED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT Currently, the FAA is not seeking formal responses to this announcement. However, the FAA welcomes any questions, comments, or concerns regarding the attached draft PWS and the contemplated acquisition strategy to achieve a fair and equal competitive award process. Feedback should be submitted for the FAA�s consideration only. Additionally, submitted questions, or any changes to the FAA�s requirements resulting from questions, may be publicly posted. Therefore, the FAA requests that any such questions submitted be sanitized of company names or any other information that identifies the requester. The FAA particularly welcomes feedback on pricing strategies that could incorporate allocable cost-of-living indexes for economic adjustment within a primarily firm-fixed-price agreement, which can be identified at the time of award to reduce post-award administrative burdon. The FAA is especially interested in strategies that allow for adjustments to be calculated, rather than renegotiated, on an annual basis that can be applied to the various geographic work locations, both in-office and remote. title: Germany – Engineering design services – Gemeinde Stralendorf - Neubau der Kindertagesstätte "Regenbogen"
description: Die Gemeinde Stralendorf (Eigentümer/Bauherr) plant den Neubau der Kindertagesstätte Regenbogen als Ersatz für die bestehende Einrichtung als eigenständiges Gebäude auf dem direkt angrenzenden Grundstück für 40 Kinder (28 Kindergarten- und 12 Krippenkinder). Durch den geplanten Neubau sollen sich die Betreuungs- und Rahmenbedingungen für die Kinder und Erzieherinnen verbessern. Im neuen Gebäude ist geplant, 1 Krippenbereich für 12 Kinder sowie 2 Kitabereiche für je 14 Kinder anzubieten, so dass insgesamt 40 Kinder die Einrichtung in Stralendorf besuchen können. Die Möglichkeit einer Erweiterung um 8 Kinder (1 Mischgruppe) soll hierbei Berücksichtigung finden. Die geplante Nettogrundfläche von 328 qm entspricht der maximal zulässigen Fläche für die Entgeldberechnung. Als Gebäudestandort wird das vorhandene Grundstück (Flurstück 135/21, Flur 2) mit einer Größe von ca. 1.600 qm genutzt, ohne die bestehenden Freiflächen und -anlagen der jetzigen Kindertagesstätte zu beeinträchtigen. Diese bleiben erhalten und sollen weiterhin als Außenspielflächen genutzt werden. Das Ortsbild der Gemeinde ist in diesem Bereich durch eingeschossige Gebäude mit Sattel- und Krüppelwalmdächern sowie Nebengebäude und Anbauten mit unterschiedlichen Dachformen geprägt. Der geplante eingeschossige Baukörper der neuen Kindertagesstätte mit den flach geneigten Satteldächern soll sich harmonisch in das Dorfbild einfügen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist die Objektplanung Gebäude gem. HOAI 2021 Teil 3 Objektplanung, Abschnitt 1 Gebäude und Innenräume, Leistungsphasen 3-9. Die Beauftragung der Stufe 1 (LPH 3-4) erfolgt sofort, die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 (LPH 5-9) erfolgt nach Bewilligung von Fördermitteln. Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 besteht nicht.

Die geplante Nettogrundfläche von 328 qm entspricht der maximal zulässigen Fläche für die Entgeldberechnung. Als Gebäudestandort wird das vorhandene Grundstück (Flurstück 135/21, Flur 2) mit einer Größe von ca. 1.600 qm genutzt, ohne die bestehenden Freiflächen und -anlagen der jetzigen Kindertagesstätte zu beeinträchtigen. Diese bleiben erhalten und sollen weiterhin als Außenspielflächen genutzt werden. Das Ortsbild der Gemeinde ist in diesem Bereich durch eingeschossige Gebäude mit Sattel- und Krüppelwalmdächern sowie Nebengebäude und Anbauten mit unterschiedlichen Dachformen geprägt. Der geplante eingeschossige Baukörper der neuen Kindertagesstätte mit den flach geneigten Satteldächern soll sich harmonisch in das Dorfbild einfügen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind Ingenieurleistungen gemäß HOAI 2021 Teil 4 Fachplanung, Abschnitt 2 Technische Ausrüstung, Anlagengruppen 4-5, Leistungsphasen 1 - 4, Leistungsphase 5-9 optional (Stufenvertrag) Die Beauftragung der Stufe 1 (LPH 1-4) erfolgt sofort, die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 (LPH 5-9) erfolgt nach Bewilligung von Fördermitteln. Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 besteht nicht.

title: Netherlands – Supply services of personnel including temporary staff – Dienstverlening inhuur derden
description: HDSR wenst twee opdrachtnemers te contracteren middels ieder een afzonderlijke Raamovereenkomst. De opdracht bestaat uit de werving, selectie en contractering van tijdelijke externe inhuur. Primair gericht op deze twee segmenten: • uitzendkrachten; • detacheringskrachten. Binnen de opdracht ligt de focus op het waarborgen van continuïteit, gezamenlijke verantwoordelijkheid binnen de driehoek van beide Opdrachtnemers en HDSR, gezonde concurrentie en partnership. Kenmerkend voor de opdracht is: • geen bulk- of generieke inhuur; • overwegend maatwerk en specialistische profielen; • hoge mate van variatie in opdrachten; • het tussenkomstmodel; opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor de toeleveranciers. De opdracht richt zich op het leveren van hoogwaardige, passende kandidaten voor veelal unieke en specialistische functies voornamelijk binnen de domeinen: • techniek binnen een waterschap; • specialisten op het gebied van water; • IT; • bedrijfsvoering. De dienstverlening die wij vragen van de beide Opdrachtnemers is: • werving en selectie kandidaten; • (rechtmatig) contracteren inhuurkrachten; • beheer en volledigheid van het inhuurdossier; • facturatie en betalingsproces; • levering van managementinformatie; • relatiebeheer en proactieve adviesrol. HDSR heeft rond de 850 medewerkers. De gemiddelde verhouding van het medewerkersbestand van HDSR is op dit moment 90% vaste medewerkers en 10% inhuur. Dit betekent dat er per jaar gemiddeld 85 inhuurkrachten actief zijn binnen HDSR. Op dit moment (augustus 2026) werken er 60 inhuurkrachten voor HDSR. Hier kunnen, onder andere voor de migratie, geen rechten aan ontleend worden. Voor de maximale looptijd van 5 jaar bedraagt de indicatieve waarde van beide Raamovereenkomsten samen: € 59,1 miljoen exclusief BTW. Het maximum bedrag van de beide raamovereenkomsten gezamenlijk bedraagt € 88,65 miljoen exclusief BTW voor de volledig mogelijke looptijd van 5 jaar. Indien deze maximale waarde gedurende de looptijd door beide Raamovereenkomsten gezamenlijk wordt bereikt, eindigt de Raamovereenkomst met beide Opdrachtnemers direct van rechtswege.

buyer: European Commission, DG DEFIS - Defence Industry and Space
title: Belgium – Research and experimental development services – EU Complementary Time (C-T) and Complementary Position and Navigation (C-PN) services
description: Satellite-based navigation and timing services are a cornerstone of Europe’s economy and critical infrastructure resilience. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications. Several studies attribute roughly 10 % of EU GDP to PNT related activities, while a single day without GNSS could have a financial impact up to €1 billion. The Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59). The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF. Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess: • How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU. • How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034. • How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required.

Das Angebot soll als vordringlichstes Ziel die Stärkung der Motivation haben. Teilnehmende bei Los 2 sind: - Leistungsbeziehende ab 25 Jahren mit wenig Motivation an den Zielen im Jobcenter mitzuwirken, durch Stillstand in der Entwicklung von möglichen beruflichen Zielen - Schulabschluss und evtl. vorhandene Berufsausbildung ist nicht relevant - Der Teilnehmende muss deutsch verstehen und sich verständigen können.
